decisions.text: **Key protocol: epoch keys in v1, MLS later.** Validated 2026-10-18: neither Apple's App Store Review Guidelines nor Google Play policy requires MLS or any specific E2EE protocol for third-party messaging apps; MLS adoption by Apple/Google concerns their own RCS messaging and DMA interoperability. What the stores do require: Apple encryption export compliance (ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption, US self-classification, French declaration when distributing in France); Google Play 2026 policies on contacts permissions (Contact Picker unless broad access is core, with declaration), child-safety standards for social apps and age restriction of anonymous/random-chat apps. Added to the compliance profiles and external services. — ADR-0003 unchanged; security §8; external services

decisions.summary: Wave 4 G accepted and merged: the e2e send flow creates its 1:1 at run time through a Node member device (E1's peer), the web stack runs on a private t_gweb_* database per run, the seed loader tolerates active OTP codes and rate limits, and every suite uses Playwright 1.64.1.
decisions.text: Wave 4 G accepted and merged: the e2e send flow creates its 1:1 at run time through a Node member device (E1's peer), the web stack runs on a private `t_gweb_*` database per run, the seed loader tolerates active OTP codes and rate limits, and every suite uses Playwright 1.64.1. Root cause behind the "released unchecked" reports of waves 4–5 (found by G): the shared dev database's policy layers had been signed with a per-worktree KMS key file that was deleted with its worktree, so every server failed policy verification and fell back to fail-open defaults. Fixed by a single shared absolute `KMS_LOCAL_KEY_FILE` for all checkouts and a reseed of the dev policy (P0-G-02-F5). The Hebrew guard gap in the dev registry and the RTL nudge flow (`test.fixme`) go to D as P0-D-01-F14. Agents run on Opus from 2026-10-19 evening after the Fable usage limit; the commit trailer follows the running model.

decisions.text: the machine ran out of RAM again with three agents and had to be restarted (swap 21 of 22.5 GB, load ~300, macOS restarting daemons). Owner: "run the agents and keep an eye on this machine not to overload it." Lead response: at most two agents at once; one Playwright/browser suite or dev server machine-wide at a time with one worker; agents check load and swap before starting one; a watchdog samples every 30 s, logs the top memory users to `~/.lucid/watchdog.log` and alerts the lead at swap > 6 GB, free < 20 % or 5-minute load > 20; VS Code workspace settings stop the editor watching and indexing `.claude/worktrees` and build output (each worktree carries ~1.5 GB of `node_modules`; the VS Code Playwright extension was also running its own admin test server). Root cause not proven; the watchdog log is the evidence for the next occurrence (ENV-F15).

decisions.title: Playwright tracing on macOS.
decisions.summary: Playwright tracing on macOS.
decisions.text: Playwright **tracing** on macOS. With `trace: 'retain-on-failure'` every test records a screencast; on macOS that memory is held by **WindowServer** and never released when the browser exits. Measured with the watchdog log and controlled runs on 2026-10-19: WindowServer 412 MB → 8.85 GB during one 16-project admin matrix (23:14–23:39); one admin WebKit phone project +515 MB and +1 GB swap with tracing, ±0 with `--trace off`; gallery suites (no tracing) ±0 in both engines. Fix: every Playwright config records traces and videos only in CI or with `LUCID_PW_TRACE=1` (verified: the same project now leaves WindowServer flat). Memory already held by WindowServer is freed only by logging out or restarting. The two-agent limit and the watchdog stay; `.vscode` watcher exclusions stay as hygiene.

Binding on message jobs is `when_present` until clients publish rosters, then `identity.roster_binding: required` (F key, E1/E2 publishing). Decisions on D's questions: (1) one reader's **invalid** roster must not refuse the whole group message (a single broken or hostile member could block a group): that reader is dropped from the wraps, counted, and their client is told to refresh its devices; a 1:1 with an invalid peer roster is still refused. D changes this next (P1-D-08-F2-F1-F2-F5). (2) A stale roster on a message job seals to the newer roster the Mediator has seen (as built); Coach and Assistant keep refusing. Receive filters reach the Mediator per reader with an interim cover encoding until B adds a cover body.

decisions.title: Wave 6 B and wave 7 F accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 6 B and wave 7 F accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 6 B and wave 7 F accepted and merged. B: device linking (the new device shows the QR so its secret never reaches the server; ADR-0016 Proposed), rotation on every membership or device change sealed only to verified rosters, encrypted backup v1, dedicated sealed-input kinds for Coach drafts and Assistant requests, Mediator-signed `AssistantEvent`, a cover body for receive filters; the live runner has 33 checks (`link.relay`, `backup.blob` skip until C serves them). F: `identity.roster_binding`, Assistant tool lists, confirm TTL and rate keys, Coach Guide rate, console controls, the 500-character T&S note. Decisions: (1) tools that cannot be undone are **private-only** and never offered in `@lucid` public (validation rule, as built); (2) changing `assistant.public_tools` needs two super-admins, `tools_offered` one editor so a misbehaving tool can be withdrawn fast (as built); (3) `identity.roster_binding` is market-level only, no cohort rollout (as built); (4) `@lucid` public replies in groups are Mediator messages in the conversation log with the ⓘ annotation mark, not side-channel events. **Owner decision needed:** should backups include the device identity key by default? Including it lets a restore continue as the same device (peers see no "security code changed") but a stolen backup plus an offline passphrase guess, or a photographed link QR plus a malicious server, could impersonate the device until PIN-protected key derivation lands (P1-B-03-F3). Lead recommendation: **off by default until P1-B-03-F3**, then on.

Decisions on the eval readiness questions (`docs/testing/evals/gate1-readiness.md`): (1) at Gate 1 fairness gaps are **reported with 95 % intervals, not hard limits** (sets are still small); they become hard limits at Gate 2; (2) Coach decline rates are measured **pooled at Gate 1 with per-language rates reported**, per-language required at Gate 2; (3) **safety** metrics (guard recall on the abuse set, manipulative-objective refusal, unsafe-alternative rate) must pass on the **95 % lower bound**, quality metrics (translation, meaning preservation, planner hit) on the point estimate. decisions.title: Wave 7 B accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 7 B accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 7 B accepted and merged. B's review found a hole in the backup-handover rule the lead gave B and C (L90/L91 messages): after a SIM swap plus re-registration, an attacker who guesses an identity-carrying backup's passphrase could continue the roster as an ordinary update (a soft "device updated") instead of the reset peers show as "security code changed". Adopted fixes: (f) the handover is accepted only if the re-registration passed a **registration lock with the PIN** (`backup.handover_requires_lock`, default true; otherwise restore publishes a reset roster); (g) the window starts at the old primary's `devices.revoked_at` so repeated re-registrations cannot extend it; (h) the handover must be created no earlier than `revoked_at − 2 min`; clients show a reset-level warning when a handover's new primary was never in the roster and the signer left. This risk applies only to backups that carry the identity key, off by default (L85, still the owner's call). Also accepted: `CoachInsightDetail.noticed` (field 7, sealed; the clear RPC field goes once D and C switch), explicit error names, live `rotation_due` event, a dedicated `assistant_reply` body for `@lucid` public replies (Mediator message, AI-generated mark signed with the envelope). Public replies stay whisper-only until E1's renderer ships.

decisions.text: Wave 9 C accepted and merged; full integration 163 passed on Railway with no dropped connections; conformance 34/0. decisions.text: Local development must not depend on Docker. The machine crashed during wave 4 (16 GB laptop; Docker Desktop VM at 12 GB plus seven parallel agent worktrees and an emulated amd64 Playwright image) and the disk filled three times. Direction: run `apps/server` natively (`pnpm --filter @lucid/server dev`) against Railway-hosted or Homebrew-installed Postgres 17, NATS and Redis, with Railway Buckets or MinIO for S3; keep Compose/Docker for CI and optional Linux-baseline runs only. The integration suite's testcontainers setup needs an external-services mode (CI already sets `LUCID_TEST_SERVICES=external` but `apps/server/test/integration/global-setup.ts` ignores it). Agent waves are limited to 2–3 concurrent worktrees; worktree `node_modules` are removed after merge. Implemented the same day as ENV-F3 (ADR-0015): Railway project `lucid.chat`, environment `dev` (EU) with Postgres, Redis, NATS JetStream and MinIO; root `.env` shared by all worktrees via `scripts/with-env.mjs`; integration tests in external mode; Docker Desktop capped at 4 GB / 20 GB and its 23 GB disk image deleted. Follow-ups ENV-F4…F7 in the checklist.

decisions.text: Wave 4 C, E1 and F accepted and merged after the crash; all verification ran against the Railway dev stack (ADR-0015). C: held-action server side (B runner 23/28, the five skips wait on frames C adopts in CT-01-F17), KMS key announce with proof of possession, Twilio Verify/Prelude/Lookup adapters without SDKs, registration lock with KMS-bound counters (library defaults until F adds `identity.registration_lock.*`, P1-C-02-F1), discovery with keyed hashes, groups, reports intake; `NATS_STREAM_PREFIX` per process (ENV-F8) is now mandatory for anything that touches the shared stack. E1: real keys against the real server (identity record, epoch-1 bundle, Mediator key record), B frames with graceful degradation when `ServerHello.features` does not advertise them, Mediator codes rendered only through `mediationText`, Mediator-signed removals verified on readers (L55), group level/scope and personal settings device-side until C serves them; React Compiler note: method calls on stable objects are memoised, so derived values go through `useLocalValue` (docs/14 lint note to add). F: compliance catalogue v1 console screens on `@lucid/ui` tokens (console copies removed, P0-E2-01-F4 F part), axe scan in every project, kill switch effective in < 0.2 s against the mock API; Playwright aligned at 1.64.1 across gallery, mobile and admin. Test adjustments for the remote stack are explicit in code (`EXTERNAL` branches: fewer racing senders, sends in rounds, longer pump waits) and never weaken assertions. decisions.text: (a) NATS per-role users on Railway are delivered as a generated `nats.conf` (`infra/nats/gen-config.mjs` → `infra/railway/nats/<env>.conf`) through a config-from-variable start command on the stock image (or the repo-built `infra/railway/nats/Dockerfile`); the existing `NATS_AUTH_TOKEN` becomes the password of the `lucid_all` user, which stays unrestricted on `dev` because JetStream API subjects carry the stream name as one token and every worktree has its own prefix (ENV-F8), so least privilege per role applies to environments with one fixed prefix (`ci`, staging, production). Server-side nothing changes for stage A (`nats://user:pass@` URLs already work); `NATS_CREDS_FILE`/mTLS stays the staging+ target (CR P1-H-06-F10 to C). (b) Observability backend for stage 0: Grafana LGTM (`grafana/otel-lgtm`) as a Railway service or on a separate EU host behind the redaction collector (`--config=env:OTEL_CONFIG`), SigNoz kept as the alternative; dashboards and alert rules are generated code (`infra/otel/grafana/build.mjs`); no observability stack on the development machine (ADR-0015). (c) The server image prunes its `pnpm deploy` tree to reachable packages (`infra/compose/server/prune-deploy.mjs`, 643 → 140 packages) instead of waiting for a pnpm 10 upgrade or a server-local DB package (P0-A-02-F11). (d) Nightly CI runs the integration suites in external mode against a Railway `ci` environment, gated on `RAILWAY_CI_ENABLED` until the lead creates it (ENV-F7).

Load runs happen only on the perf runner: `tests/load/run.sh` and `infra/compose/compose.sh` exit 3 on a development machine unless `CI` or `LUCID_PERF_RUNNER=1` (`LUCID_ALLOW_LOCAL_LOAD=1` / `LUCID_ALLOW_LOCAL_COMPOSE=1` override knowingly); the harness reads the stack from the variables `with-env` provides; e2e servers bind per-checkout ports and never reuse another checkout's server. The Gate 1 reference topology on the runner is left open (Compose `server-split` vs role processes against a Railway `ci` environment, ENV-F7/ENV-F10). Id clashes from parallel agents were resolved by renumbering: G's CT-10-F10 → CT-10-F14, P0-D-01-F10/F11 → P0-D-01-F12/F13, A's stream sweep ENV-F10 → ENV-F12, A's pnpm image closure P0-A-02-F9 → P0-A-02-F11. Per-worktree isolation on the shared stack is now `NATS_STREAM_PREFIX` + `REDIS_KEY_PREFIX` (ENV-F8/F11), and the integration project takes a fresh Redis namespace per run. Server fix found by the remote stack: the OTP resend cooldown is measured on the database clock (the Railway Postgres runs ~1 s ahead of the laptop). `merge` is an allowed commit type.

decisions.text: Wave 11 D accepted and merged (`a45f769`). Owner's L102 question answered (`docs/01-research/inference-providers-2026-10.md`, `docs/07a` §B1): open **OVHcloud AI Endpoints** (guard Qwen3Guard-8B, classify gpt-oss-20b, Assistant gpt-oss-120b, STT, embeddings) and **Scaleway Generative APIs** (translate/rephrase/clarify/explain/trust/convey/Coach on Gemma 4 26B-A4B, summaries on DeepSeek V4 Flash), plus **OpenRouter** with ZDR enforced as a cross-vendor fallback (never for EU-residency calls); Groq optional, Fireworks not needed. Expected cost ≈ $5 for the alpha (50 daily users, two weeks), ≈ $750/month at 10k MAU; a full live eval run costs cents. `.env` lines: `OVH_AI_ENDPOINTS_TOKEN`, `SCALEWAY_SECRET_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (+ `GROQ_API_KEY`); then `pnpm ai:smoke` and `pnpm ai:evals:live`. Registry profile `alpha.json` (EU first, fixed order, `dpa_on_file` gate for staging/production). First real-model evidence from OVHcloud's keyless sandbox: smoke 8/8; guard Qwen3Guard-8B recall 0.90 / FPR 0.03 / p95 1.4 s (fails Gate 1 on Hebrew abuse 0.67 and sarcastic put-downs 0.60); classify misses the 2 s limit on gpt-oss-20b; Assistant planner tool hit 0.94 with zero unconfirmed destructive steps. New compliance gap G18: Scaleway keeps request content of erroring/abusive traffic up to two weeks — counsel question; lead's view: acceptable only if the Mediator's sealed boundary is documented as extending to that vendor under its DPA, otherwise route those tasks to OVHcloud. Open for the owner: whether classify should move to the self-hosted guard GPU before the alpha (P1-A-06) given hosted timeouts.

Also: push payload v2 with the per-device alias and B's per-wake sealed seq (migration 0017), the PIN vault (client API draft.11, migration 0018; budget shared with the lock), policy audit rows with `diff_hash`/`content_hash`/`key_id`, retention aggregation (migration 0019), F helpers adopted incl. reciprocal `nobody`, `CatchUpResult.digestEvent`, `GROUP_LEAVE_BATCHED` flag (1458 → 983 ms on Railway, off until staging). **Lead decisions pending owner:** dev and staging `fail_safe.fail_open_timeout_ms` = 3000 (F wave 15 ships `policy:set` and applies it), production stays 1500 until staging measures real inference; the vault's wrong-PIN answer becomes **403 `backup_share.pin_invalid` with `attempts_left`** (a 401 on an authenticated endpoint would make token-refreshing clients loop) — C wave 13 changes it, B updates `key-backup.md`, E1 reads the code; migrations 0017–0019 applied to the shared dev database.

decisions.text: Wave 13 D accepted and merged. Held-out guard set (100 records written blind from the guidelines, answer key sealed): Qwen3Guard-8B alone recall 0.67 / FPR 0.15; with the second-opinion rule 0.73 / 0.04; Hebrew 0.44 → 0.78; sarcasm 0.20; implicit exclusion 0.00 — the wave 12 recall gains were in-sample (tier-0 cues fired on 83 % of tuning abuse, 31 % held-out); the FPR cut and the category gain hold. The escalation model alone scores 0.89 / 0.09 and catches every sarcasm case (too slow hosted today) → a stronger tier-1 guard is the path (D wave 14), not more cue rules. Second opinion now starts in parallel on a cue and is dropped after `verdictBudgetMs − elapsed − 100 ms`, so the unchecked rate equals the switch-off rate; the "provisional verdict + late second opinion" option is rejected (cannot nudge a delivered message). Verdict-path reads parallelised (421 → 141 ms at 70 ms RTT). `budget_ms` in the queue contract (C fills it). `clarify_question` live: recall 0.92 but FPR 0.67 on clear controls. **Lead decisions pending owner:** (1) alpha default: second opinion **on** with all three triggers now that the deadline exists; builds without the wave 13 Mediator must keep it off; keyed run must show p95(first)+p95(second) ≤ 1 300 ms and < 10 % late; (2) **sender clarity questions off in the alpha layers** (reader-side clarify stays on: 1.00 / 0.00); (3) recent turns for context (L100): two designs are written up in `docs/mechanisms/recent-turns-device.md` — device-attached sealed turns (D's recommendation) or the dispatcher attaching the last N ciphertext envelopes the Mediator already received (sender cannot fabricate context, no extra upload, nothing new stored); **lead recommends the dispatcher-attached envelopes**, capped by count and age, Mediator keeps nothing; B's protocol work waits for the owner's pick. Registry: OVHcloud first for the second opinion (P2-H-08-F16 done).

decisions.text: Wave 14 D accepted and merged. Guard comparison on held-out v1+v2 (160 blind records): Qwen3Guard-8B alone 0.60 recall / 0.20 FPR (falls apart on new data: sarcasm 0.10, implicit exclusion 0.13); Qwen3.5-9B with a JSON guard prompt 0.85 / 0.06 (0.95 / 0.06 when it answers; Hebrew 0.87 / 0.00) but p50 1.2 s hosted; Mistral Small 3.2 0.84 / 0.18. Both guards in parallel with Qwen3.5-9B preferred: 0.61 / 0.09 at sandbox latency, **0.88 / 0.08** at ×0.75, 0.91 / 0.07 at ×0.5; +1.38 USD per 1,000 user-days (≈ +$0.07/day at 50 users, ≈ +$410/month at 10k MAU). The second-opinion rule cannot raise recall (it fires only when the small guard hesitates). **Lead decision pending owner:** the parallel-guard setup is the alpha direction, behind `ai.guard.race.*` (F wave 19) and built in the Mediator (D wave 15), switched on when the keyed run shows Qwen3.5-9B p95 ≤ 1,300 ms with < 2 % timeouts; nothing meets Gate 1 yet (recall ≥ 0.9, FPR ≤ 0.03 per language). Sender clarity prompt revised: needless questions on clear messages 0.47 → **0.07** held-out (recall 0.93); **lead decision:** sender questions stay off in the IL/DE/US alpha layers until the keyed run confirms ≤ 0.10, then IL first. GPU sizing (P1-A-06): two L40S running both models ≈ $1,600/month; justified by latency, not cost, below ≈ 24k daily users; the 150 ms target needs H100-class cards or smaller guards. `eval_only` aliases enforced by loader, router and smoke.

decisions.text: Wave 16 D accepted and merged. **Trust card root cause (P1-G-w8-F2):** not C 16 (G's failing commit predates it; product code identical between the passing and failing stacks) — two Mediator defects: the card was planned only when the trust read returned (a failed, timed-out, switched-off or text-less read dropped the whole card), and an unchecked result arriving after the fail-open timer published no overlays; with C 16 merged the server delivers both overlays 5 of 5 on Railway. Fixed: the card is planned whenever the read was attempted (FIRST_CONTACT + metadata facts without a read), the read starts first in the deferred phase, unchecked overlays publish once per job. Verdict-path reads capped at min(250 ms, time left) counted from their own start; classify cache read after tier 0 knows the language; sender clarity's recent-turns read inside the question's budget. Guard prompt v4 (money rule rewritten; favours flagged 6 → 3 of 10, scam + guilt 10 of 10, +0.6 USD per 1,000 user-days) eval-only until held-out v5 (60 blind records, sealed) decides. `MediateInput.context` accepts recent turns from either L117 design; nothing changes until C carries a context. **Lead decisions pending owner:** route v4 if v5 passes the readiness §7 row (the cost is accepted for fewer false nudges on favours); the additive `late` overlay batch name (P1-G-w8-F2-F3) is approved for C + D. C 17: the context-less job default hides the trust card (`dispatcher.ts:174` swallows the error, `mediation-job.ts:68` defaults `firstContact` false; P1-G-w8-F2-F1). G 10: re-run `alerts.spec` ×3 on main with the server's `mediation.failsafe` / `mediation.deferred` / `t2.*` lines (P1-G-w8-F2-F2).

decisions.text: Wave 17 D accepted and merged. Held-out v5 (sealed before prompt v4 was written; one blind run on the OVHcloud keyless sandbox): v4 on the 9B guard 0.87 recall / 0.10 FPR against v3's 0.90 / 0.40, favours flagged 11 → 2, scam and guilt records answered as safe: none for either prompt; in the race with the native guard 0.93 / 0.07 before delivery. **v4 is routed** (registry `alpha-2026-10-21.4`; v1 and v3 eval-only; the race stays off until the keyed run). Lead reading of §7 "no scam or guilt record lost", pending the owner: counted on answered records, sandbox timeouts counted separately as in wave 16 (strictly, v4 13 of 15 against v3's 14 of 15; reverting is one swap of two registry candidates), P1-D-09-F4-F5-F2-F2-F2. Voice-note transcription built behind `ai.transcribe.voice_notes` (off; F adds the key; C wires a media read in the Mediator role): the transcript is used for the verdict only, never stored, cached or sent in an event; translation and conveyance see the caption only; fail-closed conversations hold a note whose words cannot be checked. Finding: Whisper turbo looped on 6 of 12 Hebrew, Arabic and Russian synthetic notes; the gateway now refuses repetition loops and fails over; those markets must not turn transcription on before native-speaker notes and a second speech candidate (P1-E1-w14-F2-F1). Late overlays now go out as batch `late` without repeating delivered (kind, reader) pairs; **deploy order: dispatcher before Mediator.** v5 is now seen; the next prompt revision needs a sealed v6 first. New open decision 0aq: whether a reader's own transcript of a voice note should exist at all (it would store the words).

decisions.title: Wave 18 E2 accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 18 E2 accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 18 E2 accepted and merged. `Composer` takes `sendDisabled` and `sendDisabledReason` (spoken, never shown); Send stays visible with its icon, is mirrored in RTL and never fires; Enter does nothing while disabled. Lead approves the new `docs/10` §5.3 "Disabled state" rule: 45 % opacity (`disabledOpacity`) for text, glass and clear buttons and settings controls; the accent Send instead takes `disabledColors` at full opacity (off track fill, off ink ≥ 3:1, 4.5:1 in high contrast, glass-line ring), because a faded accent disc fell to 1.35:1 on Sky Glass. Known deviation accepted: on web a disabled Send is out of the tab order (a native disabled button cannot take focus); the size notice is an announced status. E1 adopts it in wave 17 (P1-E2-w18-F1); H draws it in the size-notice mock (P1-E2-w18-F3).

decisions.title: Wave 26 F accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 26 F accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 26 F accepted and merged. Market-only keys `trust_safety.enforcement.{enabled, restrict_days, suspend_days}` (0 = until lifted, 0–365; two super-admins; a global layer that sets them is refused on publish and ignored when served; nothing set in the dev layers); `messages.max_payload_bytes` global 16,384, range 4,096–65,536, a market may only lower it; console decision sheet and case page show the server's enforcement state (off / no market / named markets / unreadable) and what was applied; CT-09 documents the 400 on a non-reviewer assignee and the 409 bundle without an object store. Lead approves F's strict reading (market-only, not just no-cohort). Change requests to C: enforce and serve the size key (P1-E1-w16-F1), a per-case "would apply" field (P1-F-w26-F1), object store and a reported account for the live run (P1-F-w26-F2), a lift operation outside the appeal path (P1-F-w26-F3, **approved as a contract change**, CT-09 next bump).

decisions.title: Wave 15 B accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 15 B accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 15 B accepted and merged. `AccountEventKind.ENFORCEMENT` (13) with a notice (measure, applied/lifted, reason code, end time with 0 = until lifted, the list of what it blocks so clients never infer effects from the measure's name), `ErrorCode.ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` (80) / `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED` (81) non-fatal with the notice, feature 18 `ENFORCEMENT_NOTICES`, `ServerHello.limits.max_payload_bytes` (policy value wins when present), two new live checks (`enforcement.notice`, `hello.limits`; 42 checks, 40 pass, 2 skip until C serves them), client API draft.15 as a proposal block. ADR-0017 (recent turns) drafted with both designs: **the wave 15 B brief wrongly named device-attached as the lead's recommendation; the recommendation stays dispatcher-attached (B) as in L117/L121 and open item 0** — the ADR records both and the owner picks. C wave 18 serves the notice and the limits; E1 shows the notice after that.

decisions.title: Wave 10 G accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 10 G accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 10 G accepted and merged. Desktop regression at the 3 s window green on Chromium LTR; `simswap` on WebKit 4/4 after E1 16 (the next attempt is stopped); Chromium phone full suite 27 passed, 1 failed; nightly `admin-real` job (contract-live role + F's real specs, WebAuthn pass with `--invite-out`, reporter without traces so the invitation never lands in a report, P1-G-w10-F2); web stacks stop on SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP (P1-A-w16-F1) and every e2e entry point uses `isMain` (P1-A-w16-F2). **Trust-card defect re-scoped (P1-G-w10-F1, now C's):** on 9 tapped failures the Mediator wrote the clarity and trust overlays every time (0.3–1.4 s after release, never unchecked), the server published the reader's overlay events (~1.6 s after release, no retries, no warn or error), and the browser's WebSocket never received a frame of that later batch; the scam alert sent with the verdict does arrive live; passing runs got the overlays only from the catch-up page. The loss is in live delivery of later-batch events to a device connected seconds earlier. Lead: P1-G-w8-F2 moves to C; C wave 18 takes P1-G-w10-F1 as its first item; E1 adds the one-fetch mitigation after a stranger's first message in wave 17 or 18. Also: since E1 16 every Node client of the app's code fails at start with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` (`@lucid/policy` exports need a `default` condition, F; P1-G-w10-F3); voice player time label stuck at 0:00 and "Resend code" / "Call me instead" enabled above the stopped panel (E1, P1-G-w10-F4, F6).

decisions.title: Wave 18 H accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 18 H accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 18 H accepted and merged. Mocks v1.9 (screens 137–143: size notice with the disabled Send as the target, not-sent rows with Retry and with Edit, stopped sign-in with the hold end and "The stop is over"); transcription documented in `docs/05` §3.5, `docs/12` G18 (g), DPIA inputs (R21, Q8), sub-processors (speech: OVHcloud, Scaleway, Groq; no DPA on file), privacy-notice outline; `docs/04` §9 carries the rollout order dispatcher-before-Mediator until A writes the deploy runbook (P2-H-08-F27); conformance-5 audit (7 deviations, all fixed in place); two counsel questions added (voice processed only for its words as biometric data; speech provider terms excluding voice-model training). Lead republishes the hosted mocks as v1.9 (MOCKS-w16-F1).

decisions.title: Wave 17 A accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 17 A accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 17 A accepted and merged. `security.event` outcomes `account_warned|restricted|suspended|enforcement_lifted` and event `ts.enforcement` (applied / lifted / refused only; other answers never fall back to `applied`) registered with counter `lucid_ts_enforcement_total{outcome,measure,action,market}` and a panel; nightly `cold-start` job (warm then cold, 5 × 5 at 1.5 s, after `admin-real` because Railway jobs share the `ci` prefix) with thresholds in `nightly-first-run.md` §4 and a failing summary when no round was measured; first-nightly preconditions table (none met: the GitHub repo has no branch yet, owner item A2). **Finding:** the nightly `failopen` and `cold-start` measure nothing on main today because the member device dies at load (`ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`, same cause as P1-G-w10-F3); F 27 adds the `default` export condition (root cause), G uses the runtime tsconfig in `failopen-rate.mjs` as a belt (P1-A-w17-F4). One noisy hand run with the local fix: warm p50 1,280 ms / 1 of 5 over the window, cold 1,727 ms / 5 of 5 (P1-A-w17-F6). Lead routes: `ts.enforcement` logging from the enforcement service and a non-zero exit from `cold-start.mjs` on zero rounds to C 19 (P1-A-w17-F1, F5); the busy-check self-match (a waiter whose own argv contains the pattern) to G's next wave: exclude the checking process and its parents (P1-A-w17-F2).

decisions.title: Wave 17 E1 accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 17 E1 accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 17 E1 accepted and merged. Over the size bound the app now shows Send disabled with the notice's own sentence as its spoken reason (one string for both; `role="status"` kept), proven LTR, RTL, pseudo-locale and Sky Glass light; the order-dependent search failure was three start-up races, each reproduced before its fix (`fillAllNow` returned before the session's resume was applied; it skipped gaps whose fetch was already running, so the search answered "nothing found"; a request to Lucid before keys, engine and store were open was refused): fixed with shared fetches, a readiness flag and `data-ready` on the intro; the composer's size check takes the market policy value (DE 8,192 over the global 16,384) ahead of the hello's bound (P1-B-w15-F4 done early). Full chromium-phone run w11+w13+w14+w16+w17: 27 passed, 0 failed. New: a request typed to Lucid before the device is ready is lost (P1-E1-w17-F1): E2 19 adds a "getting ready" disabled Send and extends `docs/10` §5.3; `walkthrough-w15` to wait for `data-ready` (P1-E1-w17-F2, E1 next wave).

decisions.title: Wave 27 F accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 27 F accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 27 F accepted and merged. `@lucid/policy` exports carry a `default` condition (Node peers and the nightly member device load again; root cause of P1-G-w10-F3 and P1-A-w17-F4); `ai.transcribe.voice_notes.{enabled, max_duration_ms}` as a **market-only**, two-person key (absent = off; while on: duration set, market languages declared, and he/ar/ru markets refused by a rule until P1-E1-w14-F2-F1) — lead confirms the strict market-only reading, as for the enforcement keys; console "Voice notes" section; console disabled states aligned to `docs/10` §5.3 (ghost and switches 45 %, filled primary and stop buttons in `disabledColors`); rule messages isolate bidi text parameters. Lead: §5.3 to state that `disabledColors` applies to filled text buttons too (E2 19 has it, P1-F-w27-F3); D decides whether transcription skips a note whose detected language is he/ar/ru in an enabled market (P1-F-w27-F4, next D wave); `@lucid/i18n` dist extensionless imports (P1-F-w27-F2, E2 later, no harness hits it).

decisions.title: Wave 19 E2 accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 19 E2 accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 19 E2 accepted and merged. A disabled primary `Button` takes the `disabledColors` look (track fill, muted ink, glass-line ring, full opacity) in all themes, contrast modes and RTL; `Composer` `gettingReady` disables Send with a spoken "getting this device ready" reason and no visible change; `docs/10` §5.3 lists the reasons a Send may be disabled (size bound, getting ready, enforcement notices reserved) and the rule that an on-screen notice's sentence is always the spoken reason. Gallery Chromium 131 / WebKit 131. **Lead decision (P1-E2-w19-F3, pending owner):** no second cue for disabled text buttons for now — the ring and ink weight distinguish a disabled primary from an enabled ghost on Sky Glass; revisit on a device walkthrough. E1 18 wires `gettingReady` (P1-E2-w19-F1); H adds the state to mock 137's family and redraws the disabled primary in mocks 114–121 (P1-E2-w19-F2).

decisions.title: Wave 11 G accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 11 G accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 11 G accepted and merged. Nightly `failopen` and `cold-start` measure again (member on the runtime tsconfig, kept as a belt after F 27; P1-G-w11-F1 drops it later); `scripts/lib/busy.mjs` (one `ps` snapshot, counts only node processes that run a suite or stack, ignores the checker, its parents and children and any shell that merely names a script; `stack --wait` / `suite --wait` are now rule 14's commands); `scripts/lib/stop-server.mjs` (SIGTERM to the server alone, 30 s drain, then the wrappers; all eight shutdown lines present, no force kill). **Fail-open re-measure at the 1.5 s window, 300 messages, warm-up on: 0 unchecked (95 % CI 0–1.26 %), 4/4 first messages checked, 0 late or missing verdicts, Mediator p50 972 / p95 1,317 / max 1,614 ms** (wave 9: 0.33 %, max 4,683 ms). One concern: in the 5-message smoke the very first message on a fresh stack was released unchecked and never received a verdict (1 of 305; P1-G-w11-F2) — C 19 finds the lost job (a verdict must always arrive, even late). `alerts.spec` verification waits for C 18. `apps/mobile/README.md` and `infra/nats/README.md` still show the old `pgrep` commands: E1 and A point them at `busy.mjs` in their next waves.

decisions.title: Wave 18 D accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 18 D accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 18 D accepted and merged. Held-out guard v6 (100 records, 20 per language, ten abusive/benign pairs each incl. the money pairs v5 exposed) is the first set sealed hash-first (seal commit `e5b4f7a9` before the records `057434d4`); the lead ran `heldout.ts verify --set guard-heldout-v6` after the merge: verified, 100 records, inputs `05384a30…`, key `9a1c5d18…` (P1-D-09-F4-F5-F2-F2-F3-F1 hash check done); runs and scorers refuse a sealed set unless opened by name. Keyed-run playbook `docs/testing/evals/keyed-run.md` (13-row pass/fail table, caps 0.63 USD total, expected ≈ 0.18 USD and 30 min); every keyed runner exits 3 before any call when a key is missing, naming the variable only. **Lead decision (pending owner):** in the keyed run v6 records v4's blind answers only; v6 is opened and scored once, when the "small loan with an easy no" revision is committed, scoring v4 and the revision together; a v7 is sealed before any later revision. Note: v5 was not sealed hash-first (inputs and key landed together); its result stands as a blind single run. Labels are the author's, not native speakers' (owner item A4 labelling).

decisions.title: Wave 19 H accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 19 H accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 19 H accepted and merged. Mocks v1.9.1 (144–145 getting-ready composer LTR/RTL; every disabled filled text button in the off look, ghosts at 45 %); `docs/12` G18 (g) re-run against the voice-note key as built (shape matches; still open before any market enables it: speech DPAs, native-speaker evals, the Mediator's media reader, detected-language handling, decision 0aq); `docs/06` §1 and the testing README carry the wave 9 / wave 11 fail-open figures and the nightly chain; `docs/10` §5.3 covers filled text buttons. Lead republishes the hosted mocks as v1.9.1 (MOCKS-w17-F1).

decisions.title: Wave 18 A accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 18 A accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 18 A accepted and merged. `docs/runbooks/deploy.md` (roles and env, migrations first, rollout order migrations → dispatcher → Mediator → worker → api/admin → gateway → config; key pins before keys, code before policy, consumer of an additive contract change first; gates `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `role.mediator.consuming`; rollback in reverse; Railway `staging` shape), `docs/04` §9 points at it; `pnpm docs:check` falls back to local `main`; the NATS switch scripts use `busy.mjs`; owner checklist for A2 `docs/runbooks/owner-a2-ci-staging.md` (names only, generated values piped, never typed). **Finding and lead decision pending owner (P2-H-08-F27-F1/F2):** no environment beyond the laptop can run today — the only server KMS adapter is `local` (a key file on one volume; split roles on Railway cannot share it and production refuses it), and the sealed Mediator must not run on shared infrastructure. Decision: Railway `staging` holds **test data only**; the first environment for alpha users is a dedicated small VM (or the owner's cloud account) once a real server KMS adapter exists. A 19 (with D) writes the ADR and builds the adapter: `KeyService` unchanged; master key from the platform's secret store (env/secret file) wrapping the key group kept in Postgres, key use audited (P1-A-05 first half); cloud KMS / OpenBao adapters stay later options. Added to the owner briefing as A8 and to the status board.

decisions.title: Wave 18 E1 accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 18 E1 accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 18 E1 accepted and merged. Send, Attach and Voice wait until keys, engine and store are open (Send disabled with a spoken reason; a request reaching Lucid another way is held up to 20 s, not refused); a non-contact's first message arriving live without its clarity or trust overlay is fetched once after the verified policy's `fail_safe.fail_open_timeout_ms` (no client number of its own; no verified value, no safety net); stopped-panel chips "Resend code" / "Call me instead" dimmed and inert while a stop holds; G's voice time-label finding was whole-second rounding, not a defect; the Node peer loads with the app's own tsconfig after F 27 and two stale harness checks were fixed. Full chromium-phone run w11–w18: 46 passed, 0 failed. Open: the HTTP range API returns no overlays, so the safety net works over the socket only (P1-E1-w18-F3, C 19); `Chip` has no disabled state (P1-E1-w18-F1, E2); G re-runs `alerts.spec` with the frame tap after C 18 (P1-E1-w18-F4).

decisions.title: Wave 18 C accepted and merged; migration 0029 applied to the shared dev database.
decisions.summary: Wave 18 C accepted and merged; migration 0029 applied to the shared dev database.
decisions.text: Wave 18 C accepted and merged; migration 0029 applied to the shared dev database. **Trust card defect closed on the server (P1-G-w10-F1):** the web app reloads the page when a chat opens, its socket closes ~0.3 s after the message, the deferred overlay batch is published with no socket open, and the new socket resumed with `last_dseq` 0 because the client's dseq tracker expects contiguous numbers while device dseqs are the shared stream's sequence (never contiguous), so the gateway started at the stream's end and skipped the batch. Server fix: a per-device resume point ("after the last delivered") stored at close; a known device resuming with 0 continues from it; a new device starts at the end. `alerts.spec` ×3: 1/3 → 9/9 on two runs. **Client defect remains (P1-C-w18-F2, E1 19 first item):** the app never acks and always resumes with 0, so a web connection that receives 2,000 events without an ack stalls on flow control. Also landed: `messages.max_payload_bytes` enforced per market and served in the policy document and `ServerHello.limits` (env value a hard ceiling only); enforcement notices live as `AccountEvent` ENFORCEMENT with push wake, `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` refusals with the notice, feature 18, test trigger; client API draft.15 in `components` (mobile, server, admin types regenerated); CT-09 `liftCaseEnforcement` (step-up, a reviewer other than the decider, 409 `self_approval` / `invalid_state`, audited, no Idempotency-Key yet), `CaseEnforcement.would_apply` / `state: none` / `lifted_reason`; contract-live with an object store and a seeded case naming a reported account; `media.mediator.get` presigned read with length and digest check, off until the transcription key is on; `docs/runbooks/server-deploys.md`. Live conformance 42/42 with no skips. P1-G-w11-F2 (first message on a fresh stack never decided) did not reproduce; two candidates named for C 19 (1 s epoch-bundle miss cache; a roster-binding refusal that publishes nothing). Lead approves C's edit of `infra/nats/roles.mjs` (new media subject) pending A's review (P1-C-w18-F4).

decisions.title: Wave 20 E2 accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 20 E2 accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 20 E2 accepted and merged. `Chip` (and `Button`) take `disabled` + `disabledReason` (spoken only; glass chip 45 %, selected chip in the off look; a real disabled control on web and native); `docs/10` §5.3 states Attach and Voice are not offered until the conversation is open and chips follow the disabled rule; `@lucid/i18n` dist loads under plain Node (`.js` specifiers and JSON import attributes added post-build, Node probe test). Gallery Chromium 135 / WebKit 135. E1 adopts the chips on the stopped panel (P1-E2-w20-F1, in E1 19's scope if it reaches it, else E1 20); H draws them (P1-E2-w20-F2); A may unify the two post-build scripts (ui, i18n) when convenient. Full integration run on main after C 18: 47 files, 297 passed, 1 skipped, but the vitest process exited 1 with no failed test; the lead is re-running with full output to find the cause (P1-C-w19 input).

decisions.title: Wave 16 B accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 16 B accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 16 B accepted and merged. `protocol.md` "Device stream cursor and resume" (dseqs increase with gaps; client tracks the highest applied; acks at most every `receipt_batch_ms`; resume rule for non-zero, zero-from-a-known-device and never-served devices); live checks `resume.device-stream` and `hello.policy-bound`, stricter `enforcement.notice` (draft.15 `measure` / `effects`); reference gateway numbers with gaps and keeps a resume point; **live conformance 44/44, no skips**; draft.15 as C moved it is identical to B's proposal. B's note: an event sent to a socket the client is already closing counts as delivered, so a cursor-less client will not get it again — closed by E1 19's real cursor and acks. **Integration run on main (lead):** 297 passed, 1 skipped, exit 1 from one unhandled rejection: `DrainingConnectionError` from `EphemeralHub.offline` → `presenceEvent` → NATS publish during a gateway connection close while the connection drains (gateway flow-control test teardown); C 19 makes the offline presence publish tolerate a draining connection (and audits the other close-path publishes). The same log shows `policy.resolved` errors `E_POLICY_LAYER_SIGNATURE_INVALID` on the api role during the run; C 19 confirms they come from a test that deliberately serves a bad layer, or fixes them.

decisions.title: Wave 19 A accepted and merged; migration 0030 applied to the shared dev database.
decisions.summary: Wave 19 A accepted and merged; migration 0030 applied to the shared dev database.
decisions.text: Wave 19 A accepted and merged; migration 0030 applied to the shared dev database. `@lucid/kms-envelope`: `KeyService` unchanged; envelope v1 (versioned AAD header: domain, generation, master key id, key id; AES-256-GCM under an HKDF per-domain key); keys in Postgres (`server_kms_keys`, `mediator_key_groups`); master keys from a 0600 file or a secret-store variable; production refuses `local`, key generation at start, a key file inside a git checkout, a value a `.env*` file also holds, the Mediator master key in any process that is not Mediator-only and the server master key in the Mediator; `pnpm --filter @lucid/server kms status|generate|promote|state|import|rewrap`; lint and gitleaks rules; api and gateway proven to share one key set through Postgres with the gateway as a separate process and no key bytes in its debug output. **Lead decisions:** two master keys (server, Mediator) approved — one key would let api/gateway open the Mediator's rows; ADR-0018 status set to Accepted pending the owner (envelope now; OpenBao / cloud KMS later behind the same interfaces; HSM half of P1-A-05 open); per-use key audit at debug, lifecycle at info, durable audit sink is P1-A-05-F1. H 20 updates `CLAUDE.md` repo layout, `docs/04`, `docs/07`, `key-rotation.md` (P1-A-05-F4).

decisions.title: Wave 19 E1 accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 19 E1 accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 19 E1 accepted and merged. The app tracks the highest applied dseq, acks it every `receipt_batch_ms` and resumes with it (0 only when it never applied an event); real server: 155 device events through a 32-event window with no stall, 118 acks, nothing re-applied; `alerts.spec` ×3 with the frame tap on main: 9/9 with every trust card live and the safety net unused (P1-E1-w18-F4 E1 part). Enforcement notices in the app (lock glyph toast, chat-list card, composer card, Account and security row; reason label, "Until …" / "Until it is lifted", listed effects only, "How to appeal"); Send and creating actions disabled with the card's sentence; refused sends kept unsent until lifted; 403s worded; demo knob and the server trigger. **Lead decisions:** "How to appeal" opens Consent and legal until the appeal screen exists (P1-C-w15-F1) — acceptable for the alpha, the notice's wording stays provisional until owner decision 0ab; Attach and Voice are **not** offered while sends are blocked (E1's recommendation, P1-E1-w19-F2 → E2 21 updates `docs/10` §5.3, E1 adopts); `BarAction` disabled state (P1-E1-w19-F1, E2 21); the enforcement notice mock waits for 0ab (P1-E1-w19-F3).

decisions.title: Wave 28 F accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 28 F accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 28 F accepted and merged. Console Lift action (fresh step-up worded by key type, a reviewer other than the decider, 409 `self_approval` / `invalid_state` worded, one Idempotency-Key per sheet), decision sheet uses `would_apply` (markets listed only for a pre-wave-18 role), T&S vocabulary v2 with `enforcement.lift` reason codes (`lift.decision_wrong`, `lift.new_facts`, `lift.account_compromised`, `lift.disproportionate`; lead approves the codes), fixture re-recorded against C 18 with the seeded reported account (enforcement-on live run: suspension applied as `would_apply` predicted, lift 200 `reviewer_lifted`, repeat 409). Against the role the Lift is 400 until C accepts the `enforcement.lift` codes and takes the Idempotency-Key (P1-F-w28-F1/F2) — routed to C 19, which is running: message sent.

decisions.title: Wave 20 H accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 20 H accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 20 H accepted and merged. KMS documented across `CLAUDE.md` (one line), `docs/04`, `docs/07`, `key-rotation.md`, ADR-0018 Accepted (pending owner), `docs/05` §3.4 says what is built; one deploy runbook (`deploy.md`; `server-deploys.md` a pointer); mocks v1.9.2 (disabled chips in 115/117/118/141/142, screens 146–147 selected disabled chip); five deviations fixed in place (incl. a refused Mediator result is terminated, not redelivered, and falls to the fail-safe timer). **Lead decision (P1-C-w18-F7-F1): default role rollout order = migrations → dispatcher → Mediator → worker → api/admin → gateway last** (the dispatcher creates the topology and the `late` batch contract; the Mediator must understand it before the gateway lets upgraded clients in; the gateway goes last so clients only ever meet a fully upgraded backend); C's "Mediator last" is the documented alternative, not the default. P1-A-05-F6 (decrypt_only generations not refused for signing, no retired/revoked state, no policy-key co-signing) goes to A 20 with D. Lead republishes the hosted mocks as v1.9.2 (MOCKS-w20-F1 if H filed one, else this entry).

decisions.title: Wave 21 E2 accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 21 E2 accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 21 E2 accepted and merged. `BarAction` `disabled` + `disabledReason` (45 %, spoken only); icons `undo-2` (mirrors) and `key-round`; `docs/10` §5.3: while an enforcement notice blocks sends, Attach, Voice and file-drop are not offered, Send is disabled with the notice's sentence, the draft is kept; Lift sheet rebuilt in the gallery in both reviewer states; gallery Chromium 141 / WebKit 141. **Lead decision:** no "lifted" glyph is added to the meaning-glyph vocabulary for now — a lift is a console action, not an intervention a user sees; the Undo2 disc in the console is fine (revisit if the enforcement notice ever shows "lifted" to the person, after 0ab). E1 20 adopts the header buttons and the no-Attach rule (P1-E2-w21-F1/F2); H redraws mock 124 (P1-E2-w21-F3).

decisions.title: the Opus weekly limit stopped six running workers mid-wave (G 12, C 19, H 21, E1 20, A 20, D 19; all with commits saved in their worktrees).

decisions.title: Wave 20 A accepted and merged; migration 0031 applied to the shared dev database.
decisions.summary: Wave 20 A accepted and merged; migration 0031 applied to the shared dev database.
decisions.text: Wave 20 A accepted and merged; migration 0031 applied to the shared dev database. Key-generation states `decrypt_only` (no signing, audited `denied`), `retired` (public record kept so old signatures verify; private key purged after a grace period, default 7 days) and `revoked` (refused for everything, key destroyed); `kms retire|revoke --confirm|purge|state`; a group must keep one active generation; the Mediator announces active generations only; new conversations are not assigned to `decrypt_only` groups. Append-only hash-chained `kms_audit` (trigger refuses UPDATE/TRUNCATE; per-use operations aggregated per flush; start-up records written before continuing; `KMS_AUDIT_SINK=db|log`, production refuses `log`; `kms audit --verify`). **Lead decision:** per-role grants are a `kms grants [--apply]` command, not a migration (migrations run as the schema owner; dev and CI have one database user) — accepted; the Mediator role needs SELECT+INSERT on `kms_audit` to append to the chain. One root `scripts/esm-specifiers.mjs` replaces the two package copies. Change requests: C adds the `kms_audit` retention batch (P1-A-05-F1-F1); C + E1 carry `revoked` in the `MediatorKey` DTO and clients verify with retired records and refuse revoked ones (P1-A-05-F6-F1); co-signing and server-key marks (P1-A-05-F6-F2), moving conversations off `decrypt_only` (P1-A-05-F6-F3) stay open. P1-A-05 now has only F2 (a KEK the process never holds) open.

decisions.text: the owner minted a new Railway project token (scope: project `lucid.chat`, environment `dev`; stored by the lead in `~/.lucid/railway-dev.env`, mode 600) and restated: the status site must be a **small separate server that does not depend on the app or production services**. Finding: Railway has had a major outage since 11:33 UTC ("Dashboard and API unavailable, builds paused", incident QH8L8B3E); the earlier "token not found" verdict (L194) was taken during that outage and may have been the outage rather than a revoked token; `railway add` now answers "Deploys have been paused temporarily". The backing services (data plane: Postgres, NATS, Redis, MinIO through their proxies and passwords) never needed the token and kept working all day; the token is only for control-plane actions (creating services, deploying, `nats:switch`). Lead: a retry loop creates the `status-site` service and deploys as soon as builds resume; the service is its own container with no link to the app services; a separate Railway project (`lucid-status`, own token) is the cleaner isolation and is offered to the owner. Because the token was pasted in chat, rotate it once the outage is over and write the replacement straight into the file.

decisions.title: Wave 17 B accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Wave 17 B accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 17 B accepted and merged. Client API draft.16 proposal: `MediatorKey` gains `signingStoppedAt`, `retiredAt`, `revoked`, `revokedAt` (a revoked record is also `retired: true` so draft.15 clients never use it; listing returns every record; by-id serves revoked ones); client rule in `protocol.md` §Mediator key states (pin active only; seal to active and decrypt-only; accept a signature whose object timestamp is no later than the signing stop; refuse every signature by a revoked group, revocation permanent); feature 20 and live check `keys.mediator-states`. Scope proposal contract: `ConversationUpdate.scope_proposal` with readable codes or a sealed change (both outcomes of the L197 decision representable), state machine proposed → accepted / declined / withdrawn / expired / superseded, accept writes the scope layer + ACCEPTED entry + `policy` entry in one transaction, feature 21 and live check `scope.proposal`; groups 409 `scope.not_one_to_one` for now. 46 checks (two skip until served). **Lead confirms** B's choice: a scope proposal at level Off is refused with 409 `scope.level_off` (no Mediator, no scope to mediate). C 20 serves both (P1-A-05-F6-F1-F1, P1-C-05-F2); E1 adopts the key rule (P1-A-05-F6-F1-F2) and the proposal card (P1-C-05-F3); F adds `scope.proposals.ttl_hours` (P1-B-w17-F1).

decisions.text: track Railway incident QH8L8B3E (https://status.railway.com/incident/QH8L8B3E — "Dashboard and API unavailable, builds paused"; latest update 16:29 UTC: builds and deployments remain paused, the support site is down). decisions.text: a **Twilio account** was opened and its Account SID and auth token handed to the lead ("see that it gives you all you need; 100 test SMS; close the loop or text me once"). State found: a Trial account created the same day, balance $0.00, no phone number, no Messaging Service, no verified recipients, no Verify service. The lead created the Verify service **"Lucid"** (what `TwilioVerifyAdapter` needs) and put `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `TWILIO_VERIFY_SERVICE_SID` in the git-ignored root `.env`; `SMS_PROVIDER` stays `mock` until the live smoke passes (P1-C-01-F1). Lookup v2 works on the trial (the owner's number resolves to an Israeli mobile). A test verification to the owner's number was refused with Twilio error 21608: during the trial the recipient must be a verified tester — so the loop cannot be closed until the owner verifies their number in the Twilio console (or upgrades the account). Open-decision 36 (vendor accounts + DPAs) is partly unblocked: Twilio exists as a trial; the DPA, the upgrade and Prelude remain.

Done by the lead: an organization budget of €100/month with alerts at 50 % and 100 % to the owner's email and SMS (Billing API v2); the DPA was found signed (v5, 18:42 UTC) so `dpa_on_file` is true for Scaleway in the alpha registry (reviewed in the same commit); the smoke run shows no quota refusal on the models in use. Then the owner: "put model caps as well, they do seem to be hard caps" — found the console's `generative-apis/v1/consumption-limits` API (shipped 2026-10-19, undocumented) and set per-model hard caps: 10M tokens/month (1M/day, 100k/min) on the eight models the registry uses, 100k tokens/month on the ten it does not — worst case ≈ $93/month, under the budget alerts; whisper's cap pending a Scaleway 503. The only thing still not a hard stop is the invoice itself: Scaleway bills past a budget, so the alerts plus these caps are the guard. The owner's key stays an owner-type user key with full access until the deferred rotation.

decisions.text: Guard prompt v5 result (D 19, pending merge): v5 clears the three favour conditions on held-out v6 (money favours flagged 4 → 1; recall / FPR 0.98 / 0.17 on answered records vs 1.00 / 0.25) and the three tuning favours, but **times out about twice as often as v4 on the sandbox** (tuning + held-out v1–v4: recall 0.58 vs 0.81 when a timeout counts as a miss; 148 vs 77 errors over 492 records; its prompt is 142 tokens longer). **Lead decision, closing the open reading of §7 (L166):** for routing, a timeout counts as a miss, because an unanswered guard call is a message released unchecked (fail-open) or held (fail-closed), the very failure the fail-open measurements track. Therefore v4 stays routed; v5 is eval-only; v5 is routed only if, on the keyed run, its error share is within one point of v4's and it still wins the favours conditions. D 19 reverts its registry swap before the merge. Voice notes in he/ar/ru: transcribed, relying on the gateway's refusal of repetition loops (new outcome `refused` = missing evidence, the fail mode decides; `lang` limited to he|ar|ru|other|und) — accepted. Held-out v6 is now seen; the self-talk false nudge needs a sealed v7 first.

decisions.title: Wave 21 D accepted and merged — first real-model run on Scaleway.
decisions.summary: Wave 21 D accepted and merged — first real-model run on Scaleway.
decisions.text: Wave 21 D accepted and merged — **first real-model run on Scaleway.** Registry `alpha-2026-10-21.8`, Scaleway only: guard Gemma 4 26B-A4B with prompt v4 (choice rule written before the run; Mistral Small 3.2 and Qwen3.6 as failover), second opinion Mistral Small 3.2, classify and mid tier Gemma 4, large tier DeepSeek V4 Flash, Assistant gpt-oss-120b (Llama 3.3 failed the tool probe), speech Whisper large-v3, embeddings Qwen3-Embedding-8B; the 19 OVHcloud candidates in a new `retired` list (never routed); OpenRouter and Groq removed; when Scaleway is down every call errors and the fail mode decides. Scaleway's DPA v5 is on file (signed by the owner in the Scaleway console on 2026-10-21 18:42 UTC, read through the Account API by D 19's resumed session; `dpa_on_file: true`, kept through the merge), so the profile is accepted in staging. Fleet cap `AI_FLEET_BUDGET_DAILY_USD=10` / `AI_FLEET_BUDGET_MONTHLY_USD=100` in dev (at the cap optional tasks are skipped and the rest refused, nothing reaches Scaleway; a Redis outage reads as zero spend, so the console limits are the backstop). **Results (no timeout or error in any call, so strict = answered):** guard on tuning + held-out v1–v4 (392 records) 1.00 recall / 0.00 FPR in all five languages, p95 0.43 s (sandbox 9B guard: 0.81 / 0.06 strict); held-out v5 blind 0.93 / 0.00, 0 of 15 favours flagged, 15 of 15 scams caught; second opinion fits the deadline (p95 0.90 s) but its `controversial` trigger lowers recall — keep it off (F); classify 1.00 / 0.00 at p95 0.85 s; Assistant planner tool hit 0.97, 0 safety misses, p95 3.97 s against 3 s (D next); Whisper large-v3: no repetition loops in he/ar/ru, WER he 0.11, ar 0.06, 0 elsewhere — the he/ar/ru hold-back can be reconsidered after native-speaker notes; clarify Arabic recall 0.75 below 0.8. The synthetic sets are saturated: native-speaker labelled sets are the next guard evidence (owner item, labelling vendor). Spend 0.384 USD of the 2.00 cap. Owner steps: enable seven models with monthly limits summing to ≈ $100 (Gemma 4 ≈ 250M tokens ≈ $75; gpt-oss-120b ≈ 65M ≈ $12; Mistral Small ≈ 28M ≈ $5; Qwen3.6 ≈ 9M ≈ $3; DeepSeek V4 Flash ≈ 4M ≈ $2; Whisper ≈ 575 audio minutes ≈ $2; Qwen3-Embedding ≈ 8.6M ≈ $1), budget alerts at $50 and $90, rotate the key. Open for the lead: `docs/07`'s two-vendor rule vs L223 and G18 (P1-D-w21-F6). Merge note: a test import lost in the auto-merge was restored by the lead.

decisions.title: Wave 19 C accepted and merged (partial on one row).
decisions.summary: Wave 19 C accepted and merged (partial on one row).
decisions.text: Wave 19 C accepted and merged (partial on one row). Shutdown hygiene: best-effort publishes (presence, typing) and NATS replies after an `await` drop quietly while NATS drains (content-free debug record + count); `stop()` waits up to 5 s for connections; the `E_POLICY_LAYER_SIGNATURE_INVALID` log lines are two deliberate bad-layer tests, now asserted. Lost first verdict (P1-G-w11-F2, **partial**): `cold-start.mjs --fresh` reproduced it on 3 of 4 first fresh stacks and then 0 of 17; root cause not pinned; a Mediator guard now never acks a job without a verdict while retries remain (redelivery 2/5/10/20/40 s, then a warning; a delivery running past 120 s is given back); `cold-start.mjs` exits 3 on zero rounds (P1-A-w17-F5); a dispatcher-side watchdog for a job that never reaches the Mediator is proposed (P1-C-w19-F3). `ts.enforcement` logged (P1-A-w17-F1). `MessageRange.overlays` on the HTTP range API (P1-E1-w18-F3; client API stays draft.15, additive). CT-09: lift accepts only the v2 `lift.*` codes; `Idempotency-Key` with `Idempotent-Replayed` and 409 `conflict` on a different body (P1-F-w28-F1/F2 C parts). Four full integration runs on a slow Railway day (59–69 min each) each had one different failure (a cold first message without a verdict; a 1.5 s window miss in re-registration; a gateway resume timeout; NATS API timeouts in setup); none was an unhandled rejection; live conformance 44/44 each time. Main's `apps/admin` `wave20.test.ts` has one expected failure until F 32 removes the lift from `IDEMPOTENT_AHEAD_OF_ROLE` (its conditional item, now live). Lead: G 16's real-inference runs and the next full run on a calmer stack decide whether the gateway timeout was C's change; A registers `nats.publish_dropped` and the late-verdict outcomes (P1-C-w19-F1); the redelivery schedule as a `fail_safe` policy key (P1-C-w19-F2) is F's next wave.

decisions.summary: Wave 23 A (Fable) accepted and merged; migration 0032 (kms_master_keys) applied to the shared dev database.
decisions.text: Wave 23 A (Fable) accepted and merged; migration 0032 (`kms_master_keys`) applied to the shared dev database. ADR-0019: OpenBao Transit as the first KEK the process never holds (one named non-exportable key per domain; with `LUCID_KMS_KEK=transit` each domain's master key rests in `kms_master_keys` as Transit ciphertext and the process unwraps it once at start under its own identity; envelope rows, generations, states and `kms_audit` unchanged); `TransitClient` (token file / AppRole, CA bundle and SPKI pin, bounded timeout, retries only on transport failures, no response body in errors, token in a closure); `kms rewrap --to transit|file` in one transaction; production refuses `env` master keys, `http://`, a token variable and the other domain's key name per role. **Threat model recorded honestly:** keys are still unwrapped in process memory while running; what moves out of reach is the KEK, so a database copy plus a leaked secret store no longer opens a key; a process start needs OpenBao up and unsealed. **Lead decisions:** production refusing a master key in a variable stands (Railway therefore runs production only via `transit`, consistent with L179); migration 0032 accepted; ADR-0019 as its own ADR. Open: run the real `bao` half once (P1-A-05-F2-F1), provision OpenBao on the alpha VM with the seal decision (P1-A-05-F2-F2, owner), cloud KMS adapter later (F2-F3). 68 package tests, 418 server unit/contract tests, 35 integration tests green.

decisions.text: Wave 16 G accepted and merged — **the whole stack on real inference for the first time** (Mediator on `alpha-2026-10-21.8`, ≈ 950 real calls, no errors, no refusals, no fleet-cap hit, ≈ 0.26 USD). Holds: fail-open **0/300 unchecked at the 3 s window** (Mediator p50 1.27 s / p95 1.72 s / max 2.23 s), first messages 4/4 checked, cold start still 0 unchecked, trust card live 3/3 (1.1–1.7 s), `chat.spec` and conformance green. **Does not hold:** at the 1.5 s window 7/300 unchecked (2.3 %, 2 of 30 hostile lines) and 3 verdicts never arrived; **scam lines are held at the sender as a nudge instead of being delivered to the reader with a scam alert** (0/6 alerts; the mock did 9/9 — a product-rule violation: scam and manipulation alerts are reader protections, product plan §3.2b); a harmless ≈ 10 KB message is held (en and he); the sender clarity question is never asked (0/3) and a clarity note reached a Hebrew reader in English. **Lead decisions:** the fail-safe window for the alpha is **3 s** (closes item 0e for dev/staging and the alpha; production stays decided on staging with real traffic); D 22 (Opus, mediation pipeline) fixes the scam mapping, the long-message hold and the clarity trigger with real-model tests before any further Gate 1 claim; C looks at the three verdicts that never arrived and the six unchecked burst messages (P1-G-w16-F5); A/C log the registry source and version at Mediator start (F1); G renumbers the fail-open script so "(88)" cannot appear (F6); E2 moves the member device's scope import off React Native (F7, done by the new subpath when adopted). decisions.text: Railway incident QH8L8B3E is still *Identified* (builds and the API down); Railway published a **security disclosure dated 2026-10-21** with per-service guides. What applies to Lucid: the dev stack's **Postgres and Redis use the Railway templates with public TCP proxies for local development**, so their passwords count as possibly exposed. **Decision:** as soon as the control plane returns, before any suite runs against the stack, a Fable agent (L198, security-sensitive) regenerates the Postgres and Redis passwords with the dashboard's *Regenerate* (never by hand inside the database), pastes the new `DATABASE_URL`/`REDIS_URL` values into the root `.env` (and the integration/e2e variables that carry them), rotates the NATS and MinIO credentials we set as Railway variables, runs `pnpm env:doctor` and `pnpm db:migrate`, and records the rotation in `docs/runbooks/dev-environment.md`; the owner then mints a fresh dev-scoped project token (`~/.lucid/railway-dev.env`) in case project variables were readable. Checked today: no Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Grok, Stripe or GitHub credential of ours is stored in Railway variables (the Scaleway key lives only in the local `.env`); the status-site retry loop was re-armed (third six-hour window). Owner item added below.

decisions.text: Wave 24 D accepted and merged; **guard prompt v6 is the routed guard prompt on Gemma 4** (registry `alpha-2026-10-22.2`) because the pre-registered self-talk rule passed all four conditions on the one-time v7 opening (verify passed; seal → records → prompt → rule commit order checked; 760 paced calls, 0 errors, 0 timeouts, 0.208 USD; Gemma quota 13.30M of 15M left). Numbers: held-out v1–v4 recall 1.00 for both, v6 one extra false nudge (ru teasing slice, `guard-ru-926`); v7 false-positive rate 0.22 (v4) vs 0.18 (v6), recall 1.00. **Lead reading:** the rule was followed as written (L226), and v6 is equal or better on every set but one record, so the routing stands; but **self-talk is not fixed** (both prompts flag 9 of 15 self-talk records; v6's gain is on caring replies) and both fail the gate1 false-positive limit on v7, so Gate 1 stays *not ready* on this row. Decisions: the Mistral and Qwen failovers, the second opinion and the launch backstop stay on v4 until v6 is measured there (P1-D-w24-F2); the next revision is a **v8 aimed at self-talk with a freshly sealed held-out v8 before any tuning** (P1-D-w24-F1), and the native-speaker labelling of a larger self-talk set (open item on labelling vendor) is the real unblocker. decisions.text: Wave 25 D accepted and merged. **Held-out v8 sealed hash-first** (seal `916d5488` before records `06cab1dc`; 120 records, 24 per language, aimed at self-talk, caring replies, self-harm pushes carried by self-talk and the `guard-ru-926` teasing class; inputs `929ceb4d…`, key `2baf7679…`; the lead re-ran `verify` after the merge), then prompt **v8 draft** (v6 plus one self-talk sentence, narrowed self-harm intent clause) as eval-only candidates in registry `alpha-2026-10-22.3`, then the pre-registered **Self-talk rule v8** and **Failover rule v6** (`evals/wave25-rules.ts`), then the runs: on the seen sets (tuning, v1–v4, v7 as regression) v8 keeps recall 1.00 and cuts false nudges from 10 to 2, clearing all 15 v7 self-talk records and `guard-ru-926` while adding two new ones; **v8 was not opened**. Failovers: the rule failed on Mistral Small 3.2 (Arabic misses 5 → 7, one v7 self-harm push missed) and Qwen3.6 (Spanish misses 3 → 5), so **the failovers, the second opinion and the launch backstop stay on v4**; pooled failover recall 0.89–0.93 against Gemma's 1.00 is a finding (P1-D-w25-F2). Gateway: `ai.call` events carry `fleet_capped` (day | month | none) and the CostMeter counts capped calls (P1-A-w28-F3 gateway side; A registers the counter, P1-D-w25-F4); `outcomeClassOf('RATE_LIMITED')` is `rate_limited` (P1-A-w28-F4). **Lead accepts deviation 1** (the two-line server change keeping a 429 in the failure log via `isProviderFailure`, with the test adjusted): it is the change the row asked for. Spend 0.738 USD / 2,952 calls; Gemma 12.23M left today, Mistral 4.04M, **Qwen3.6 52k of 1M** (its cap was not raised in L243; the peer session is asked to raise it to 5M/day, P1-D-w25-F3). **Lead decision (P1-D-w25-F1): held-out v8 is opened once, now**, by the pre-registered step in the run README §5 (240 calls, ≈ 0.07 USD), because the set exists to decide v8 and the rule's conditions (1)–(4) need it; wave 26 D runs it, applies the rule, and routes v8 on Gemma only if the rule passes (failovers untouched); if v8 is routed, a held-out v9 must be sealed before any further prompt change.

decisions.text: Wave 23 E1 accepted and merged: the **first real-AI walkthrough** in the browser (Chromium phone, en / he / en-XA, 14 flows × 3 passes; WebKit composer pass; 0.051 USD) — plain exchange checked in 3.5–4.1 s, trust card 0.2–0.8 s after a stranger's first message, translation 文 ≈ 0.5 s after the original, Assistant whisper with Undo, Relay approve-first and the Strict-group hold behave as the mocks say; the reader-side clarity bubble appears on real AI. One app fault fixed: onboarding languages never reached the server (P1-E1-w23-F1). Differences from the mocks are model behaviour, filed as rows: the scam line is held at the sender instead of alerting the reader (F2, with D 22's scam-mapping fix), the sender clarity question never fires (F3, D 22), Coach adds facts, fails its first call and takes 4–5 s (F4), the Assistant asks "to whom?" instead of showing the confirm card (F5), the Strict threshold lets the English accusation through (F6), the Hebrew Relay draft keeps a softened jab without a "part left out" mark (F12) — F4, F5, F6, F12 go to wave 27 D after D 22; no hook slows inference, so fail-closed under slow inference is unwalked (F7 to C, F8 then E1); the Relay sheet's three actions truncate at phone width (F9, E1 24); `@lucid` public replies are off in the dev policy (F10, F 34 adds a dev layer); the Mediator's spend and registry facts are logged only at start and dropped by the schema (F11, A / C). Stranger's first English message released unchecked twice on a freshly started server: more evidence for P1-G-w11-F2 / P1-G-w16-F5 (C 21 is on it). iOS and Android still unwalked (no toolchain, owner item A1). Lead decision: the real-AI verdict replaces the mock-only claim on the status page; Gate 1 stays *not ready* until D 22's fixes and F4–F6 are re-walked. Wave 24 E1 launched (F9, scope settings and proposal cards on draft.16 per P1-C-w20-F4, `tier` kept in the e2e spend sink P1-A-w28-F2, push alias v2 wakes P1-B-w11-F2).

decisions.summary: Wave 26 D accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Wave 26 D accepted and merged. **Held-out v8 opened exactly once** by the pre-registered step (verify passed; seal `916d5488` < records `06cab1dc` < prompt `51a8ad73` < rules `77826036`; `--open` passed exactly twice, once per score; 240 calls, 0 errors, 0.0712 USD; Gemma 11.95M of 15M left today). **Self-talk rule v8 passed all five conditions**: on held-out v8 recall 1.00 for both prompts, false-positive rate v6 0.18 → v8 0.02 (he 0.08 → 0, ar 0.33 → 0.08, ru 0.25 → 0, es 0.08 → 0, en 0.17 → 0), no encouragement lost (50 of 50), teasing slice 0 → 0, seen sets 10 → 2 false nudges; p95 0.29 s. **Guard prompt v8 is routed** on Gemma 4 for `guard` and `guard-json` (registry `alpha-2026-10-22.4`; v6 stays the eval-only baseline, the duplicate `guard6` alias retired); failovers, second opinion and launch backstop stay on v4 (L249). Gate 1 reading: v8 passes latency, timeouts, recall and the slice gap; it still fails the false-positive limit in **Arabic only** (one benign Arabizi self-talk record, `guard-ar-1052`), so the guard row of Gate 1 is *nearly ready* and the labelling vendor (native speakers, larger sets) remains the unblocker. **Rule from now on: held-out v9 is sealed before any further guard prompt change** (P1-D-w26-F1). The lead fixed the stale mentions D 26 flagged (`docs/07` hosted-guard row, `docs/11` §4 and the new waves 25–26 paragraph, `.env.example` registry comment, the `heldout.ts` comment).

decisions.title: Waves 21 C and 22 D accepted and merged.
decisions.summary: Waves 21 C and 22 D accepted and merged.
decisions.text: Waves 21 C and 22 D accepted and merged. **C 21:** the fleet spend read `getAiSpend` (admin API `1.0.0-draft.2`; the budget store's own `b:f:d:` / `b:f:m:` counters, the cap from policy under the env ceiling, `counters: shared | process_local | unavailable`, never a zero it did not read), `sendToSent` outcome typed, OTP step-up failure code logged, B 19's CR1 (a departed proposer's proposal expires and cannot be accepted; accept re-checks membership) and CR2 (YAML names the three codes, `ConversationPolicyPatch` closed; **proposal versions stay strings** because the protocol carries them so — lead agrees, an integer would split HTTP from the protocol). **Security-relevant finding, fixed:** the three verdict-less fail-open releases of wave 16 G were a dispatcher race — a verdict arriving just after the window was read while the record was still `sent`, the timer committed the unchecked release, and `applyOutcome` returned `late` without the late path, so **a Mediator BLOCK could have left a message delivered unchecked**; `ReleaseService.afterLostWrite` re-reads once and applies the outcome as late (a BLOCK becomes `blocked_late` plus a tombstone); the repro test fails 3 of 4 without the fix and passes on main; the same signature explains P1-G-w11-F2. **D 22:** engine v1.2.0 — the needs_attention fallback applies only when the guard named no category, so `scam` (a reader risk with no level-table row) reaches the reader as the scam alert (44/44 on the real registry) and long benign text the guard calls `spam` is delivered (16/16) while long text with an insult is still nudged (8/8); the clarity question was not a trigger fault (the test line named the part of the day, which the clarify rules exclude) — a realistic pickup line asks 20/20 in five languages, and E1's 0 of 6 was the dev market layer with sender questions off (L117); reader notes get a script check and are translated or dropped; Mediator and Coach calls carry `fleet_budget`; the Redis cache test polls the write (5/5 on Railway, also on main). Lead accepts D's edits to G's `held.spec`, the Maestro flow and D 20's tuning set (the brief allowed them). **Lead actions:** `MEDIATOR_EVIDENCE_CACHE=redis` with a fresh key set in the root `.env` so the dev fleet cap is shared across Mediator processes (`env:doctor` run); production must refuse `off` (A 30). Gate 1 reading: the real-model behaviours D 22 fixed no longer block a Gate 1 claim; what remains is the Coach, Assistant confirm card, Strict threshold and Hebrew Relay draft rows (D 27), phones, staging and labelling. Waves 27 D, 22 C and 30 A launched.

decisions.text: Wave 27 D accepted and merged; the four real-model faults of the E1 23 walkthrough are fixed with before/after probes on registry `.4` (258 calls, 0.096 USD, no 429): **Coach** — the MOTIVATING goal line and few-shots made the model add deadlines (5 of 6) and put goal codes into `principle_codes` (all 17 invalid first answers, then a repair-and-failover chain of 2.5–3.5 s); the prompt is revised in place (no-new-facts rule, codes tied to their list, shots that keep their facts in five languages), the gateway normalizes code lists, and an `addedFacts` backstop drops any suggestion that adds a number, day, date, time or amount (result `unavailable`, code `ADDS_FACTS`) — 24/24 first-attempt in 0.5–1.0 s; **Assistant** — the planner treated "no chat named" as the current chat only with a state code the app never sends; a pronoun or no name now means `current` and `validateStep` fills it — confirm card 24/24, nothing runs before the tap; **Strict** — not a guard gap: the real guard tags the accusation line `manipulation` 0.6 in en and he, and engine v1 treated `manipulation` as reader-only risk at every level; **engine v2.0.0** holds `manipulation` at Strict like abuse (Use / Edit only), Gentle / Standard / Relay unchanged — **lead decision pending the owner's confirmation (new open-decision row via H 28)**; **Relay** — the convey prompt had no shots; jabs are now left out entirely with one plain left-out code per language, `stripped_codes` normalized — mark 12/12, jab kept 0/12. Arabic clarify in both mocks; a v9 guard prompt plan (length or repetition alone is never spam) waits for held-out v9. Lead accepts the deviations (draft prompts revised in place; one-token HTTP mock change; additive task-schema caps; `unavailable` instead of a new decline reason until the client has text). Routed: P1-D-w27-CR1 catalog text for the manipulation hold to E2 27; P1-D-w27-CR2 (a state code with every Assistant turn) and P1-D-w27-F1 (browser re-run) to E1 after wave 24. After the merge: mediation 660, gateway 407, mocks 95, server unit 499, typecheck clean.
