decisions.summary: Wave 20 B accepted and merged: LUCIDGR1 v1, the sealed group-rules format in crypto-formats (packages/core seal / open / Mediator-open / verify, protocol parse and check, vector with three cases reproduced by both providers and the independent noble implementation): one ciphertext for members and…
decisions.text: Wave 20 B accepted and merged: **`LUCIDGR1` v1**, the sealed group-rules format in crypto-formats (`packages/core` seal / open / Mediator-open / verify, protocol parse and check, vector with three cases reproduced by both providers and the independent noble implementation): one ciphertext for members and the Mediator keyed by a fresh `r`, `r` wrapped to the group invite key `G` (members) and to the Mediator key group, a **signed key commitment** so a writer cannot show the Mediator different rules than the members read and a server-made Mediator wrap does not open (both holes of the interim app format), AAD bound to conversation id, policy version, `G` generation, Mediator key-group id and writer; readers refuse a blob whose policy version is not below the served one and any rollback; the Mediator reads topic and rules only, never `G`. **Lead decisions:** (a) the format keys on the generation of `G` rather than the conversation epoch key, as B argues (prospective members read the rules before joining; late joiners never get older epoch keys); the disclosed cost — a former member who kept `G` reads later rules until the invite key is reset — is accepted for the alpha and recorded in `scope.md`; H updates docs/04 §4.4 and the YAML wording (CR3's text); (b) **migration: re-seal on the next admin save, no reader accepts both formats**; the Mediator treats an interim blob as no rules (its Mediator part is unauthenticated); the dev stack holds 0 rules blobs and 0 key backups, no app is released; (c) **`ifPolicyVersion` is required with `rulesEnc`**; (d) a level change to **Off is refused while a member is in a minor age band**, under a policy key (never hard-coded), dormant until `age.active`; (e) **CR5 approved as client API draft.17**: a served write for a group's level (owners and admins, within `levels.offered`, `ifPolicyVersion`, one transaction with the `policies` version, the `level_change` entry and the `policy` entry; entering or leaving Off makes the epoch stale so the change is enforced by key material). P1-B-w9-F3-F1 blocked until E1 drops the v1 backup upgrade path (CR4). Wave 23 C launched on Fable (security-sensitive: CR3 server verification of `rulesEnc`, CR5, the slow-verdict log lines, the group join preview's language fallback). E1 adopts the format and drops the interim pair in its next wave (CR1, CR4); D reads the Mediator's part (CR2).

decisions.text: Wave 23 C (Fable) accepted and merged. **Server verification of `rulesEnc`** with public data only: `ifPolicyVersion` required, `checkGroupRulesBlob` then header checks (writer = calling user and device, policy version = `ifPolicyVersion`, Mediator key group = the conversation's current one) then `verifyGroupRules` under the caller's registered key; 422 `scope.rules_invalid` with closed codes, never blob bytes; the server never holds `G` or `r` and opens nothing; **the interim app format is refused from now** (L263 b) — the app on main gets 422 `interim_format` when an admin saves rules until E1 adopts the format (E1 26, urgent, no users affected); the blob and the writer's rosters ride the Mediator job (P1-D-w29-F2 C part filled). **Group level write served** (client API draft.17, feature 23, migration 0034 `conversations.stale_epoch` applied to the dev stack): 1:1 → 409 `level.consent_required`, member → 403, outside `levels.offered` → 422, **Off with a minor member → 422 `policy.locked` under the policy key `age.minors_locks.protections_locked`** (dormant until `age.active`), one transaction with the `policies` version, the audit row, `level_change` and the `policy` entry; entering or leaving Off makes the epoch stale (`EPOCH_STALE`, detail `mediator_presence`) so the change is enforced by key material; live conformance **50/50**; migrations 24/24. Lead decision: **no `rotation_due` prompt reason** for `MEDIATOR_PRESENCE` (C's deviation accepted; the `level_change` entry is the prompt; P1-C-w23-F2 closed). Slow-verdict log lines and the join preview's language fallback done. Routed: E1 adopts the level write and rotates on `EPOCH_STALE` (P1-C-w23-F3), F an optional dedicated minors' level-lock key (P1-C-w23-F4), A a level-change event and counter (P1-C-w23-F5). decisions.text: Wave 19 G accepted and merged: the **first k6 smoke runs** (LT-01 connect storm 100 connections, LT-02 fast path 20 pairs at 5 msgs/s, LT-03 fan-out at 8 and 64, LT-04 mediation mix) on the shared Railway dev stack with mock models — 0 lost, 0 duplicated, 0 unchecked across 2,700 messages, 100 % connections ready; every latency is dominated by the ≈ 66 ms round trip to Postgres and Redis (send→sent p95 1.46 s, send→checked p95 4.6 s, server CPU 2–7 %), so **the SLOs still await staging (A2, L179)** and the dev stack serves correctness and A/B comparisons only. Design facts the run exposed: an accept is a chain of about 17 serial round trips (a per-conversation ceiling near 0.8 msgs/s on dev, P1-G-w19-F1, C), three store reads run serially on the verdict path (P1-G-w19-F3, C/D), a released message's verdict is recorded ≈ 1 s after the release (F2), receipts fall behind as the rate grows (F4). **The 1.5 s regression is explained:** the sealed stores on Redis add three serial round trips (+195 ms) to the verdict path, which predicts 8–11 % of verdicts after the timer's release point against the 10 % measured; in region this is 1–2 ms, and the alpha's 3 s window is unaffected (P1-G-w18-F1 answered). Harness fixes: the stale protocol bundle (CI trigger routed to A 35), `AUTH_MODE` leak from the shared `.env`, sampler processes. k6 installed with Homebrew, no Docker. After the merge: load 102, bundle check in sync, typecheck clean.

decisions.text: Wave 22 B accepted and merged: **`LUCIDGK1` v1**, the invite-key share — the new key `G'` sealed to every current member device (never to the Mediator: a `mediator:` device id or the key group's box key is refused and tested), a public **key check** `BLAKE2b-256(key = G, TBS(group-key-check, conv_id, generation))` that ties a generation to its key, a signature over the canonical fields (conversation, generation, `after_seq`, signer, key check, every wrap), adoption rules (`groupKeyAdoption`: never lower, exactly one up, else `rollback` / `gap` / `equivocation` / `not_current`), vectors `group-key-share.json` (`106739a9…`) reproduced on both providers and opened by the independent noble code; core and protocol functions; `protocol.md` §Invite key reset now *approved, not built* with feature 24, the server transaction and decision table, re-share and initial share, the join check (P2-H-08-F46 closed). **Lead confirms B's four deviations:** (1) a `catch_up` exception — a device more than one generation behind may jump to the generation the server currently serves if the key check matches (a lying server can deny, not substitute); (2) an initial share at generation 1 records the first check (the creator posts one right after creating the group — E1); (3) the signature covers canonical fields and wraps carry the user id so the server can check "every member reached" without a lookup; (4) the live check waits for C's endpoint. **Approved as contract change for C 29 (after C 28): `POST /v1/conversations/{convId}/group-key`, `ConversationUpdate.group_key` (field 13), `SERVER_FEATURE_GROUP_KEY_RESET` 24, `Conversation.groupKey` / `JoinPreview.groupKey`, with the migration (generation, check, recipients per generation)**; the client API version number is C's to pick once draft.18 (level proposals) is on main. Routed: E1 (reset, re-share, join check, adoption — P1-B-w22-CR2, E1 29), F (`groups.invite_key.reset_on_removal` `auto` / `reset_on_leave` `off` — CR3, F 38), H (mocks — CR4), B (a platform title format, share splitting above 1,024 devices — F1, F3). Routed: `RowLabel` weight option so the chat menu's level glyph can be tint (P1-E1-w28-F1, E2), the key-check adoption once C serves the reset (F2, E1 29), the misleading "only admins" text when a device lacks the group key (F3, E2 + E1). decisions.text: Wave 34 D accepted and merged: the roster-pin read now runs alongside the tier-0 store reads (evidence cache, classify cache, tension), with **a gate before any gateway call, any reader read, any write and any result** until the binding is known; events are held so a refused job emits exactly what it did before; one of the three dev round trips is saved (pooled 200 vs 200: commit→verdict p50 1,179 → 1,124 ms, p95 1,492 → 1,454 ms), the third sits inside the gateway (a `prefetch` of the guard's cache and budget reads, P1-G-w19-F3-CR1, worth ≈ 1–2 ms in region — deferred). **Lead confirms the security reading (invariant M34):** a message may be decrypted inside the job before the roster binding resolves because the sending key is the same key the binder checks and a refused job makes no model call, no store write and no result; the plaintext of a refused job is never retained or logged. **Measurement-validity finding:** the sealed stores ignore `REDIS_KEY_PREFIX` on the shared dev Redis, so two stacks running the same corpus within ten minutes share guard evidence and skip the guard — C 29 namespaces the sealed stores in development and the nightly fail-open script sets a fresh cache key id per run (P1-G-w19-F3-F1). decisions.summary: Wave 20 G accepted and merged: device minting in chunks of 50 with retry and a resumable manifest (328 devices in 114 s; the 256-member LT-03 now runs: 3,825 deliveries, 0 missing, 0 duplicates, 45/45 verdicts), receipt metrics in the fast-path scenario, a receipt-lag analysis script.
decisions.text: Wave 20 G accepted and merged: device minting in chunks of 50 with retry and a resumable manifest (328 devices in 114 s; the 256-member LT-03 now runs: 3,825 deliveries, 0 missing, 0 duplicates, 45/45 verdicts), receipt metrics in the fast-path scenario, a receipt-lag analysis script. **Finding for C (P1-G-w20-F1):** receipt lag follows the number of readers with receipts waiting, not the message rate (≈ 0.77 s per extra reader at a fixed rate; a 256-member group's readers held every other conversation's receipts on that gateway for minutes) because the gateway's batcher applies each reader's receipts one after another in its own ≈ 11-round-trip transaction every 500 ms; fix: one transaction per conversation per cycle, conversations in parallel under a bounded pool, fewer round trips per receipt, content-free cycle metrics — rough dev capacity ≈ 1.2 receipt transactions/s per gateway, in region ≈ 45–90/s, which alpha × 10 can exceed; C 29. The load package's protocol bundle, stale again after wave 22 B's protocol change (before A 35's CI job existed on a pull request), is rebuilt on this branch. decisions.text: **Internal-secret rotation done** (ENV-RAILWAY-ROTATE, Fable agent, d321286c + docs swept into 6b1e7d0d): MinIO root keys, the NATS token (start command now reads `$NATS_AUTH_TOKEN`, no literal), the status-site password, the eight local server secrets (admin session, token signing, contacts HMAC, OTP pepper, telemetry hash, test auth, evidence-cache key k1→k2, stub master key) and all eight KMS aliases rolled to `*-v2` with v1 kept decrypt/verify-only; every stored policy layer re-verified unchanged; old MinIO keys 403, old NATS token refused, old status password 401. Findings: four of the local secrets are read by no code (the KMS aliases do those jobs — docs to say so), the stub master key wrapped nothing on dev, 32 users and 115 OTP rows from 2026-10-18 were already unreadable under the shared key file (left as they are), 60 discovery hashes miss until clients re-upload, seven stale `t_*` test databases exist. Verified: env:doctor 5/5, db:migrate, integration smoke 4/4 twice, admin 421 passed. **Owner, dashboard only (item 0ds):** Postgres and Redis → Config → Connection → Regenerate (no CLI or API offers it; paste-safe one-liners in docs/runbooks/dev-environment.md §Credential rotation), with no stack running; then mint a fresh dev-scoped project token into `~/.lucid/railway-dev.env` and delete the old one. Follow-up P1-A-ENV-RAILWAY-ROTATE-F1: `infra/nats/switch.mjs` must deploy via `serviceInstanceDeployV2` after a start-command change (`railway redeploy` reuses the old manifest). Lead lesson: two actors committing in the main checkout share one index — the agent's staged files went into the lead's commit; from now on agents commit nothing in the main checkout, the lead commits their files for them.

decisions.text: **Merged B 24** (3fe0352e): review of C 28 as merged — six non-blocking findings P1-B-w24-CR1–CR6, the row-lock fix confirmed correct with a caveat that matters for the folds: it holds only because the lock and the joined policy read are two statements under READ COMMITTED; a fold that joins the policy row in the locking statement would read the old row and let the loser overwrite the winner (CR2, sent to C 30 as a rule: lock first in its own statement, then the folded read/write, no isolation level on write paths). Lead decisions on the rest, routed to C 29: CR3 re-check `expires_at` under the lock (level and scope), **CR4 authorization before idempotency** (a non-member gets the same 404 everywhere; this reverses the order B itself prescribed in P1-B-w23-CR3 (a) — the lead accepts B's reasoning), CR1 a race test that proves both requests waited on the lock (`pg_stat_activity`), CR5 feature flags 24 and 25 gated on the migration journal, CR6 protocol text (expiry before store, list of 20, 403 before 409). Also merged: `scopeProposalLimit` mirror in `packages/protocol` with the full drift test restored (protocol 953), `scope.md` §Configuration documents the limit, protocol.md §Invite key reset heading says approved / built by C 29.

decisions.text: **Merged B 25** (7d7a6111, Fable — the one Fable worker of the night, justified by what it found): the security review of the invite-key reset as served. **Blocking finding P1-B-w25-CR1:** the caller's role, the member list and the share decision are computed before the transaction and only the generation and check are re-validated under the row lock, so a membership change committing in that window is invisible — a member removed meanwhile keeps a wrap and the new key is sealed to a former member's device, which is the very thing a reset-on-removal exists to deny; a member added meanwhile silently gets no wrap; a just-demoted admin's reset passes. Fix (routed to C 31, to be re-reviewed by B): re-read the caller's membership and the members under the lock and re-run the decision there, with a race test. CR2–CR5 (link generation, rules blob vs key-group change, the `initial` kind's admin-trusted check, `after_seq`, a route rate limit) non-blocking, routed with it; CR6 confirms the rest as designed, the server never holds `G`. Also merged: live check `groups.key-reset` (the 52nd; 52/52 pass on the dev stack against the real server) with four reference-server faults, and the group checks kept within the per-proposer limit under L328's semantics. Lead answer to B's question: **CI and gate runners seed fresh users per run so no check ever skips**; a skip with its reason is acceptable only for an ad-hoc run against a persistent fixture (G: the nightly conformance job seeds fresh). E1 must not ship the reset flow (E1 31) before CR1 is fixed and re-reviewed. Post-merge: protocol 963, server unit + contract 606, gen:check, load bundle, docs:links 755.

Reading: since the release fold (C 30) a forged notice's refusal drops the timer row in the same statement, so when the notice beats the 100 ms ticker there is no third (ticker) refusal to count — the invariant the test should state is "both forged notices refused and the record untouched" (≥ 2), with the ticker's refusal optional. Routed to the next C wave as P1-C-w33-F2 (test fix after confirming the reading against the fold; if a refusal is genuinely lost rather than never attempted, that is a server finding). The board's tile says 404/406 with the cause.

decisions.title: Current, best-supported technology; TypeScript stays on 6.0.3, 7 when the ecosystem is ready.
decisions.summary: Current, best-supported technology; TypeScript stays on 6.0.3, 7 when the ecosystem is ready.
decisions.text: **Current, best-supported technology; TypeScript stays on 6.0.3, 7 when the ecosystem is ready.** The owner first asked for TypeScript 7 at once ("never use old or deprecated technology"), then corrected the stance the same hour: 5 is not deprecated; the goal is "optimally supported, well understood, stable and the current state of the art, not something too experimental"; 7 "is definitely preferred" if it works well with React Native and gives better performance, "but not as unequivocally as I stated"; when a new major "breaks a lot of well supported and widely used software and packages we use, don't upgrade so quickly"; look at community feedback and issues, not only package metadata. Lead assessment (sources in ADR-0020): TypeScript 7.0.2 is the Go compiler with the 6.0 language; it ships **without the programmatic compiler API**, so `typescript-eslint` (8.72.0, peer `<6.1.0`) cannot load it until TypeScript 7.1 and a typescript-eslint release built against it (draft PR over IPC exists); Expo prepared TS 7 resolution in SDK 56 but had a 7.0.2 `app.config.ts` crash (expo#47627) and its templates still ship 5.9; the 7.0.x tracker shows declaration-emit regressions (non-deterministic union order #64589, unbound type parameters #64614, unbounded memory #64708, stale incremental `.d.ts` #64809). Our repo uses no deprecated compiler option, so it is 7-ready as code. **Decision:** stay on 6.0.3 (ADR-0020); adopt 7.x when (a) typescript-eslint has a stable release supporting it, (b) Expo's current SDK documents support, (c) the declaration-emit issues above are closed in a 7.x patch; A re-checks monthly and records a `tsgo --noEmit` readiness probe (speed and error parity) in `docs/runbooks/dependency-currency.md`. The rule generalises to every dependency (CLAUDE.md "Current, best-supported technology"; `docs/briefs/_common.md` rule 16): current maintained majors, nothing deprecated or end-of-life, no early jump that breaks well-supported peers; blockers recorded with a dated re-check. **A 46** (brief `docs/briefs/wave46-A.md`) builds the dependency currency board and a `pnpm deps:check` that fails on deprecated packages; it launches after A 45 when a slot frees. Open-decision row 0eb tracks the TypeScript 7 trigger.

Counters for discovery, invites, group changes, registration lock, OTP fraud refusals and T&S lifts are registered from existing log lines; **at the C 38 merge the lead checks that C does not also increment them directly** (double counting). Under L390 A notes Railway runs nats-server 2.10.29 while 2.15.x is current: A 46 assesses it on the dependency currency board (the dev-stack NATS image is the owner's Railway template; the switch runbook decides the upgrade path). decisions.title: Fable review of wave 28 B: no blocking finding; four should-fix before anyone builds on the formats.
decisions.summary: Fable review of wave 28 B: no blocking finding; four should-fix before anyone builds on the formats.
decisions.text: **Fable review of wave 28 B: no blocking finding; four should-fix before anyone builds on the formats.** S1 the suggestion-reference tag binds D's normalized `text_key`, so inserted bidi overrides or zero-width characters still earn ✎ (fix: bind the exact text hash too; no reference is minted yet, so the body version bumps freely); S2 `checkSuggestionRef` throws on an empty held id or bad `textKey` instead of refusing (a forged reference on an ordinary message would throw inside `mediate()` and, in a fail-open conversation, release the message unchecked — exactly what the design forbids); S3 `replaced_msg_id` is unsigned when `notes` is empty, so a dispatcher or DB insider could forge ✎ against a publisher that trusts `verifyOutcome` alone (fix: sign the tail whenever either field is non-empty and make verifiers require clean notes); S4 the "older clients ignore the new fields" sentence is wrong for outcomes carrying a note (a rollout gate: dispatcher and clients on ≥ wave 28 protocol before D emits notes). Notes N1–N9 (skew default 0, language keying, title read bound, migration window, split races, block timing channel, `releaseEnvelope` key-id rule, commit the vector generator, core test needs the protocol build). Everything else verified sound: domain separation, unforgeability, sealed-body opacity, outcome framing, LUCIDGT1 construction, share split coverage, vectors re-derived independently in Python byte for byte. **B 29** (`docs/briefs/wave29-B.md`) fixes S1–S4, N3, N7, N8, N9 and writes rows for D, C, E1; it launches at the next slot and precedes P1-B-w28-CR1…CR9. **A 50** (GitHub go-live) launched now in the slot the review freed.

Still before the first push: zod 3.25.76 inside `@expo/cli` (no fixed 3.x; every Expo CLI 58.1.x depends on it) keeps the audit gate red, so **A 52** adds expiring audit exceptions (`.github/audit-exceptions.json`, an exception blocks again on its re-check date), the `railway-ci` secrets upload script (dry-run) and a full `ci:local` run; then the lead pushes, applies protection and uploads the CI secrets.

decisions.text: **Wave 32 E1 merged** (24383a28; mobile 607, i18n 210, e2e 149; real-server browser walkthrough 3/3 in en, he, en-XA): rotation after a member removal and on an identity reset, the primary-device handover (no rotation, no security-code change), own message-key grants in the link hand-off and the backup (a linked device opened its user's own Relay original), server-held blocks (`blockUser` / `unblockUser`, 403 `user.blocked` verified), APNs sandbox from config, the fail-open window set through `policy:set`, the Coach chip time (median en 1.45 s meets 1.5 s, he 1.63 s does not). **Major finding (P1-E1-w32-CR1):** on the real server a newly linked device cannot verify handed-over epoch keys because `GET /v1/conversations/{id}/keys` serves only bundles wrapped to the calling device — 5 handed over, 0 accepted, so history from before the link stays unreadable; the demo backend hid it. P1-B-01's acceptance is re-opened. **B 30** (`docs/briefs/wave30-B.md`) decides the safe served form with a threat model (membership window, removed members, the backup path) and writes C's exact change; C builds it next. decisions.summary: Waves 30 B and 36 E2 merged; the second GitHub run was red on admin timeouts.
decisions.text: **Waves 30 B and 36 E2 merged; the second GitHub run was red on admin timeouts.** B 30 (403fee38): a linked or restored device verifies handed-over epoch keys against the **full signed bundles of the epochs its user's devices were wrapped in** (option a of the threat model: the bundle signature covers every wrap, so a reduced header cannot verify; nothing is served the user did not already have; a removed member gets 404; a re-added member never gets the epoch it missed; a restore months later works because C records per user which users an epoch reached). Core refuses a grant whose bundle names none of the user's roster-history devices; feature 27 `EPOCH_BUNDLES`; live check `keys.linked-history` (53 checks) passes on the reference server and skips on the real one until C ships P1-B-w30-CR1 (`epoch_recipients` table, `listEpochBundles`), then E1 P1-B-w30-CR2. Lead merge fixes: the live conformance test expects 53 with exactly that skip allowed while the feature is not advertised; k6 bundle regenerated. E2 36 (9c00a47a): opaque glass fallback for sheets on iOS/Android in all three themes (AA and AAA high contrast measured, 0 failures in 868 pairs per theme) and the sheet height cap measured against the window (it had stopped 10 % short, which let the composer show under it); `scopeHold.suggestion.sendOnly` in five catalogs; the status tick stays in the native accessibility tree; console toasts re-render on a locale change and stack at most two. Second GitHub run (40038214173): the colour fix held; two admin unit tests ran past Vitest's 5 s default on the 2-core runner (1.7 s locally) — `testTimeout` 15 s (ENV-GITHUB-F16); the gallery engine step is A 53's (ENV-GITHUB-F15). Both rows are in the CI-health tracker.

decisions.title: A latent Vitest 5 race caught by ci:local before it reached GitHub.
decisions.summary: A latent Vitest 5 race caught by ci:local before it reached GitHub.
decisions.text: **A latent Vitest 5 race caught by `ci:local` before it reached GitHub.** Vitest 5 (bumped in A 46) keeps one fs module cache at the repository root's `node_modules/.vitest-cache` and clears it whenever the lockfile hash changes; turbo runs each package's Vitest in its own process, so after B 30's lockfile change every package cleared it at once and four suites died with `ENOTEMPTY` at startup. Fix: `fsModuleCachePath: 'node_modules/.vitest-cache'` in each package's config (19 configs; two minimal new ones for `tests/load` and `tests/mocks`), verified by a forced parallel run of the whole graph with a fresh cache (no `ENOTEMPTY`). A guard that every new Vitest config sets it goes to A (ENV-GITHUB-F17). The currency board missed `@noble/ciphers` in `packages/protocol` (B 30): refreshed. The live conformance allowance and the admin timeout of L409 ride the same push. Lesson for briefs: a dependency major bump must run the **parallel** test graph once (`pnpm turbo run test --force`), not only per-package suites.

decisions.title: "Why are we wasting time on pushes and builds and all that?
decisions.summary: "Why are we wasting time on pushes and builds and all that?
decisions.text: **"Why are we wasting time on pushes and builds and all that? Whatever we can run and do locally should be done locally. The key is to get the product completed and tested. We don't have any production or users. We only go through the CI chain if it is more efficient, not if it wastes our time in waiting."** Lead: the per-merge `ci:local` → push → watch cycle stops. Verification is local: the whole test graph at every code merge (`pnpm turbo run test`), build / typecheck / lint, `api:check`, docs and evidence checks; GitHub gets a push **once a day at most**, unwatched, as an off-machine backstop (the nightly and the admin WebKit shards run there because they cannot run here cheaply); the CI-health tracker records only what a daily run shows, no same-hour fixes; no agent time goes to CI cosmetics until the product audit's gaps are closed (the GitHub rows ENV-GITHUB-F3/F6/F7/F8/F18-F3 and the nightly's first run are demoted to "when convenient"). `docs/14` §8 updated. **Wave 47 H merged** (3089d487): a dated verdict on all 413 open rows — 30 done rows closed with evidence, 5 duplicates, 144 follow-up-blocked, 31 Android runs due, 121 blocked on another row (62 of them Phase 2 rows on INT-1), 82 on the owner or a person; all 40 sampled `done` rows hold; 1 386 of 1 696 rows done, 310 open, 107 owner-blocked / 203 schedulable (29 Android runs, 48 Fable); each merged wave on 24 Oct opened ≈ 7 rows and closed ≈ 5 — closing, not opening, is the measure now. Lead fixes from H's findings: the generator treats "blocked on <row>" as owner-blocked when that row waits on the owner (F4); `ci-health.md` no longer says nothing was pushed (F2); owner cards 0ei (control edge on blurred sheets) and 0ej (SEEN after an unblock) added (F5); item 13 lists the remaining Xcode steps now that Xcode 27.1 is installed (F3). H's major finding F1 — **no row deploys the server roles to Railway `staging`**, so every in-region measurement waits on the k3s host (0at) — becomes A 56 (brief to follow). C 41 launched.

decisions.title: answers, and a new rule for asking.
decisions.summary: answers, and a new rule for asking.
decisions.text: **answers, and a new rule for asking.** The rule, verbatim: "you only ask me about things that have deep down-the-line implications. Small things, or things where it's not clear what to decide properly — make them a setting and a configuration. Things that have bigger implications — explain them with context and I will decide. Small decisions — make them into settings, very small and easy to change — decide yourself. Don't come back to me with any variation of tens of questions again; grouping them with little context is not better in any way." On the en-bloc confirm cards: "only ask about items that are hard to decide otherwise later or have a significant overflow — otherwise you decide" — so **every `confirm` row (134) is closed as the lead's decision**. Infrastructure confirms (confirm-A): "overall yes, but not if it starts adding a bunch of extra external services; if this can be done well on Railway and represents good engineering, maintainability and recovery — yes, otherwise do better" → principle recorded in CLAUDE.md: Railway-first, no new external service without the lead's written case. **Decisions:** 35 — the domain is **belucid.chat** (bought); the lead sets the bundle id to `chat.belucid` (the reverse-DNS form of the domain itself; the owner corrected the first wording `chat.belucid.app`, L427), hosts `api.` / `app.belucid.chat`; the owner provides a zone-scoped Cloudflare DNS token through the intake page (card rewritten with the exact token scope). 0ba, 0ct, 1, 0ei, 0ea (the avatar is the symbol), 28, 0az, 0dy, 24, 0ej, 0cc accepted. **0aq reversed:** voice-note transcripts are **kept** ("needed for context, search, translation"), user-encrypted, as part of the context architecture. **0ed reversed:** a blocked sender sees what WhatsApp shows (one tick, never delivered) — a policy key `blocks.blocked_sender_mark` (`sent_only` default | `delivered`), C adjusts (L425-F1). **20:** automatic mediated sessions may be turned off by **mutual agreement** when both had agreed to enable, bounded by context and age — policy keys `sessions.auto.user_off` (`mutual` default | `never` | `either`) with `never` forced for minors by the age layer (F, D, E1; L425-F2). **0e rejected as a global rule:** "review and provide the answers and guards; we cannot set these before we have expectations for processing rates; we might allow the user to decide in some cases depending on context and who we are talking to; definitely not a global give-up-and-send" → the fail-open release-unchecked path of ADR-0009 is redesigned (Fable wave FS-1: options with guards, per-context behaviour, measured rates first). **0 (context) widened:** "we need an encrypted context in a more general sense, with memory and learning, stored user-encrypted but usable by the system: collecting relevant context and dispatching it to the AI, searching history, answering questions about earlier things … a Fable agent to propose a good-quality architecture for deeper AI capabilities common in modern AI chat tools" → Fable wave AI-1 (ADR). **12 and 0bv widened:** "device migration, using it on web like WhatsApp, backup and restore must work, cross-OS; a Fable agent to research this properly, including the AI context data"; recovery: "a clear and clean catastrophic recovery mechanism, ideally biometrically tied to my phone and someone else's, comprehensive while safe" → Fable wave DC-1 (multi-device incl. web, backup / restore / migration, social + biometric recovery of the server KEK, ADR). **0eg:** no paid GitHub plan — "figure out a better automated chain on Railway" → A row L425-F4 (the nightly suites as a Railway cron service or a self-hosted runner there). **0ef:** the repository will be shared with other developers one day → rewrite the commit before the first one gets access (L425-F5). **33:** "you should have the key, I minted a full account key" → A creates the Railway Bucket with the account token (L425-F6). **7:** "not sure what you are asking at all" → the card is rewritten with the cost (≈ 200 h, USD 4–6 k). Later: 0ee, 0dt, 36, 16, 0q, 0r, 0j. **The decisions page is rebuilt**: only material items with full context, one card each, no en-bloc cards (L425-F7).

decisions.text: **"We don't have chat.belucid.app — we only have belucid.chat, so only under this domain."** The lead's `chat.belucid.app` was the reverse-DNS bundle identifier of the host app.belucid.chat, not a domain — a confusing notation. Corrected everywhere: the bundle id is **`chat.belucid`** (the reverse of the domain itself, which Apple and Google accept), universal links / app links and the domain-bound OTP use **`belucid.chat`**, and every host is a subdomain of it: `api.belucid.chat`, `app.belucid.chat`, `status.belucid.chat`. No other domain is ever used.

decisions.text: **Product audit #4 merged** (f567b649; `docs/testing/walkthroughs/P2-H-10.md`): 284 requirements of `docs/02` §3 / §5 / §6 against the running product — **52 built and walked on a device, 103 built but never walked on one, 63 partially built, 47 not built, 19 built differently**. The critical mechanisms hold: sealed mediation (plaintext on devices and in the Mediator only; zero-retention providers; content-free logs by lint; the production process split has never run), sender control (no verdict rewrites words; ✎ only after acceptance; Relay approve-first; the user's auto-convey choice never reaches the Mediator — fail-safe but not what the user chose), Mediator-gated release (no counter-path found; the one release function refuses Relay originals and timeout releases in fail-closed conversations), platform policy (signed, layered, two-person; the lint does not cover the app or the console; eight controls store values nothing reads), visual first (the kit cannot compile a button without an icon; eight app screens use raw pressables), i18n/RTL (Hebrew walked; no literal-string lint; ar / ru / es still machine translations), compliance profiles (no country conditional in source), Coach (private, words change only on Use; the Coach profile is server-readable — DPIA note corrected). **Lead routing of the findings:** the eight plan corrections CR-1…CR-8 are approved as wording changes (H 48); the messaging basics the plan promises and nobody built — reactions, replies, edits, delete, forwarding, star, location and contact sharing, video — become a program starting with **B 32** (wire formats and mediation rules, Fable review after) then C / D / E1 / E2 / F rows; the eight dead controls, the auto-convey choice and the appeal record → **C 42** (then D, E1); the lints and the busy-check race → **A 57**; the 26 app flows that never ran on a device → **G 24**; the Android Lucid-chat defect (every request answers "can't act right now") and the two-tap country picker → added to E1 35; the console against its real admin role → the next F wave. These are Phase 1 gaps, not Phase 2: the audit is the work list until the next audit.

decisions.text: **Waves 47 F, 46 D and 56 A merged** (0505e968, 703ea1a1, da33c401; whole graph 35/35 green). F 47: the owner's settings as policy keys — `blocks.blocked_sender_mark` (`sent_only` default), `sessions.automatic.user_off` (`mutual` default; the path is `sessions.automatic`, not `sessions.auto`, to keep one section) and `age.minors_locks.auto_session_user_off` forced to `never` by a coherence rule that holds whether or not a market's age mechanism is on; console rows in six locales. Lead decision on F's question (small, L425 rule): add the rule that a market may offer `off` in `sessions.automatic.user_allowed_prefs` only where `user_off` is `either` (row to F, P1-F-w47-F1 → F's next wave). D 46: the interim Coach forms are gone from the Mediator RPC contract and the role; the suggestion-ref check carries a closed `gate` field; the confirmation's wait counts in `p95_verdict_ms` (decided, `docs/06` §1). **A 56: the server roles run on Railway `staging`** — one service `lucid-server` with all six roles, built by Railway from the server Dockerfile, private networking to Postgres / Redis / NATS, keys and policy seeded, the 3 s fail-safe window published (global v2); health and readiness green; the CT-10 acceptance run against the deployed gateway 100 sent / 100 acked / 12 held correctly / 1 206 deliveries / 0 errors; live conformance 54/54 against staging's databases; **first in-region numbers: send → ack p50 89 ms / p95 150 ms (Standard 1:1), send → checked 121 / 183 ms** (the same accept measured from the build machine to dev: 359 / 437). Deviations accepted: `NODE_ENV=development` + `LUCID_ENV=staging` (the config refuses `staging` as NODE_ENV), the real alpha model registry with a USD 0.20 daily cap (mocks are refused on staging by design), the 3 s window approved under L239 until an admin directory exists on staging. Lead decisions: the collector and Grafana on staging (≈ USD 10–15 a month, a Railway service — Railway-first) approved, A's next wave; `deploy.md` marked in use. Cost so far: ≈ USD 0.03 of model calls, ≈ USD 3–6 a month for the service. Launched: **C 42** (the eight dead controls, auto-convey to the Mediator, appeals, the blocked-sender key) and **A 57** (policy lint for app and console, literal-string lint, icon check, the busy-check race).

decisions.text: **Contract change approved for C 42** (the Mediator queue contract is shared by C and D; changes need the lead): two optional, additive fields on the mediation job — `sender.relay_mode` (`approve_first` | `auto_convey`, the sender's effective choice already bounded by policy: `relay.available`, `auto_convey_allowed`, never with a minor; the server computes the bound, the Mediator may only narrow) and `sender.protections` (`nudge_sensitivity`, `lucid_may_speak`: what the sender's own messages get); **refined the same hour at C's proposal:** stranger screening and cultural notes are reader-side choices, so they go on `readers[]` (`stranger_screening`, `cultural_notes`) next to `manipulation_alerts` / `clarity` — each reader's own choice bounded by their market's policy, applied per reader, never per conversation — with toWire/fromWire and a round-trip test; no Mediator behaviour change in C 42; D honours them in the next D wave (P1-C-w42-CR1). This is the piece the product audit found missing: the user's Relay choice and protections finally reach the Mediator (sender control as the user set it, within policy).

decisions.title: FS-1 merged (merge): ADR-0023 "Fail-safe behaviour when the Mediator is slow", accepted by the lead with its two owner questions as cards 0eq (may a sender release their own unchecked message, bounded) and 0er (automatic resumption during a long outage).
decisions.summary: FS-1 merged (merge): ADR-0023 "Fail-safe behaviour when the Mediator is slow", accepted by the lead with its two owner questions as cards 0eq (may a sender release their own unchecked message, bounded) and 0er (automatic resumption during a long outage).
decisions.text: **FS-1 merged** (merge): ADR-0023 "Fail-safe behaviour when the Mediator is slow", **accepted by the lead** with its two owner questions as cards 0eq (may a sender release their own unchecked message, bounded) and 0er (automatic resumption during a long outage). Measured first, as the owner required: on dev with real inference the verdict p50 / p95 is 1.27 / 1.72 s and 10 % of messages exceed 1.5 s (2.3 % went out unchecked at a 1.5 s window, two of them hostile); in region on staging send → checked is 121 / 183 ms for tier-0 and 435 / 788 ms for 100 distinct real messages, 0 of 300 unchecked; the binding ceiling is the provider quota (≈ 20 000 mediated messages a day fleet-wide). The rule replacing ADR-0009's "or on Mediator timeout": a fail-open message is released only on a signed PASS, on the **sender's signed release where offered**, or on an automatic release **only where a market set it** (`fail_safe.slow.auto_release`, default `never`); fail-closed unchanged; no crypto change. New states S1–S10 (glyph `checking`), the reader's standing preference (`contacts_now` default, locked to `wait` for minors), telemetry with a page on any automatic release under `never`, a 30-day staging gate. Rollout: F (keys, console predictor) → B (`ReleaseUnchecked` frame) → C + D (dispatcher ask / release, the Mediator's `slow` notice) → E1 → E2 mocks → G/A in-region p99 and cold-start measurement → a staging outage drill. ADR §10's document changes → H 50. The three architecture waves the owner asked for on 2026-10-24 (AI-1, DC-1, FS-1) are all accepted the same day; six owner cards carry their real decisions.

decisions.title: 7 — no labelling vendor: "complete bullshit … evaluate it based on work you find online … use your Opus 5.5 workers to label content and context.
decisions.summary: 7 — no labelling vendor: "complete bullshit … evaluate it based on work you find online … use your Opus 5.5 workers to label content and context.
decisions.text: **7 — no labelling vendor:** "complete bullshit … evaluate it based on work you find online … use your Opus 5.5 workers to label content and context. Search for good open conversation databases in multiple languages, download them, label them properly with Opus so we can evaluate the quality of the lesser engines we are using (smaller context, faster). Build up a good database as this will be used later as well." → program **EVAL-DB** (D 47 first): open-licence multilingual conversation corpora (he, ar, ru, es, en), a labelling pipeline run by Opus agents with Lucid's labelling guidelines, agreement measured against the 245 human-labelled records, the set versioned and reused for every guard eval; no vendor budget. **13:** Xcode's iOS platform is downloading; "the rest should be workable for you now" — the lead checks and runs the first iOS run when the runtime is present. **0ek — reversed:** "there's no such thing as an 'off' phone. We should be available in the background … like WhatsApp's web mechanism: keys still work via the device itself; access and notifications are managed with the device's help; actions are driven in the app anyway, so these are background processes done on the device. The same applies to memory and searches — move these resources and load to the end device. Our servers focus on orchestration, backup … Memory lives on the device; we will need smart mini-RAG mechanisms to score and map context and standard scored search; these should work well and fast on modern phones. This decision should be reviewed and implemented with its other implications by a Fable model and propagated across relevant features and architecture." → **no Mediator-held memory items**; device-resident memory, index and RAG; a background-execution model for the phone (the Fable wave states iOS's real background limits and what needs a wake-up push or a companion) — **ARCH-2** (Fable) amends ADR-0021 and propagates. **0el:** "the AI may remember what you know — whatever you have access to, never something you don't. The other side's Mediator may know things you don't and they are never shared; what was visible in your conversation or context may be saved. The agents may know what you know." → memory scope = the user's own visible context, quotes and all; never cross-user Mediator knowledge (closes 0el; ARCH-2 writes it in). **0em:** "not always two people; one trusted is enough, but allow me to change this later to a two-person mechanism; at this phase simplicity is preferred" → the owner alone can recover (his phone share + the offline share), the second person's share is a backup, upgradeable to a two-person requirement by moving the offline share (ARCH-2 amends ADR-0022). **0en — reversed, strongly:** "server restart must automatically restart — what kind of bullshit is this. Servers restart all the time and clusters change — of course auto-unseal … no complex account management. Find a reasonable solution that can be easily hardened later." → **automatic unseal at start is required**; no new provider account; the lead's direction to ARCH-2: for the alpha the simplest sound option is the per-domain master key (or the unseal material) held in Railway's own encrypted service variables, read once at start (the ADR-0018 shape, with ADR-0019's production rule relaxed to "a Railway-hosted stage"), hardened later by cloud-KMS auto-unseal when a provider exists; ARCH-2 chooses between that and OpenBao with the shares as Railway variables of the unseal agent, and writes the hardening path. Lesson recorded with the L425 rule: when a recommendation implies operational toil (people in the restart path) or a budget, say so in the card's first sentence.

decisions.text: **ARCH-2 merged** (the owner's L437 directions into the ADRs; no question left for the owner): ADR-0021 §13 — **no Mediator-held memory items in any phase**; memory items, the FTS and vector index, markers and scoring live on the devices (FTS5 + int8 256-d vectors, a two-stage scorer with policy weights; ≈ 50 MB per 100 k messages, native 5–15 ms per query, estimates until measured), the server orchestrates with opaque work tickets and content-free wakes and backs up opaque rows and `C_u`; **memory scope = what the user could see** (own released messages, own Relay originals, annotations returned to them; never the other side's originals, held or blocked content, or the Mediator's state about others), quotes with provenance allowed; the phone **wakes, never schedules** (iOS background push ≤ 2–3 an hour and 30 s, nothing after a force-quit; Android high-priority FCM through Doze) so time-bound features are local notifications and companions can be workers. ADR-0022 §12 — the owner's phone share plus the offline envelope recover alone, the second person's share is a backup, two-person control is one step (move the envelope); **automatic unseal is mandatory**: for alpha and beta the per-domain master keys come from Railway sealed service variables at start into 0600 tmpfs files, no human in the restart path (invariant **K18**), ADR-0019 decision 6 relaxed to exactly this form on a Railway-hosted stage, Keyholders become disaster recovery of an escrowed recovery key, hardening to OpenBao static seal (optional) and then a cloud KMS when a provider exists. **L179 is superseded for the KMS boundary**: the alpha does not need the dedicated VM for keys; Railway's sealed variable store is the stated root of trust at restart. Rows ARCH-2-F1…F10 for A, B, C, D, E1, F, G; **H 51** applies the document edits (brief committed).

decisions.text: **Wave 32 B merged** (4e8fc6ef; protocol 1 192, core 736 on both providers, mediation 906, server 704; live conformance 58 checks, 54 pass + the four new `messaging.*` skipping until C advertises them): the messaging basics the plan promised and the audit found missing are now on the wire — reply / quote, reactions (a key derived from the target's, exactly its readers, never through the Mediator), edits (mediated like a new message, combined with a subkey of the original's key; ⚠ survives, ✎ / 文 / ⓘ do not carry over), delete for everyone (author-device signature against the verified roster; a never-released message withdrawn with no log entry), forwards (sealed provenance, re-mediated under the destination's rules, "written by Lucid" only on a verified note, never the original author's name), place and contact cards, video as media; features 28–32, vectors from a committed generator, four live checks. **Security finding by B (unverified until the Fable review):** in fail-open conversations nothing binds the Mediator's key wrap and the readers' key wrap to the same message key; the AEAD is not key-committing, so a modified client could show the Mediator harmless words and readers other words — a mediation bypass. B added `checkSenderWrapK`; **D 48** (launching) runs it on every fail-open envelope and blocks a mismatch; a key commitment in the envelope is the v2 fix (B). **Fable review** of the whole wave with this finding first (`docs/briefs/review-b32.md`). Lead decisions on B's two questions (small, L425 rule): earlier versions of an edited message are **not** shown (the owner corrected the lead's first call the same hour, L442: "message edits are not commonly shown in any messaging app; we are not reinventing these behaviors") — only the current text with an "edited" mark; no policy key; a forward never names the original author (confirmed: provenance shows hops and the AI marking, not people). `messaging-basics.md` indexed in the mechanisms README.

decisions.title: "Earlier versions of edited messages are not visible.
decisions.summary: "Earlier versions of edited messages are not visible.
decisions.text: **"Earlier versions of edited messages are not visible. Message edits are not commonly shown in any messaging app. We are not reinventing these behaviors."** Rule recorded for every such call: where every mainstream messenger behaves one way, Lucid behaves that way — no setting, no variation; the lead does not invent behaviour for the sake of configurability. Applied: an edited message shows only its current text with an "edited" mark; readers never see earlier versions; the Mediator keeps the original only as long as its own verdict path needs it (B's format keeps edit history on the device as the same message's versions — E1 shows one). P1-B-w32-F2 re-decided; no `messages.edit_history_visible` key.

decisions.title: Fable review of wave 32 B: the wrap_k mediation bypass is confirmed and blocking; nothing else blocking.
decisions.summary: Fable review of wave 32 B: the wrap_k mediation bypass is confirmed and blocking; nothing else blocking.
decisions.text: **Fable review of wave 32 B: the wrap_k mediation bypass is confirmed and blocking; nothing else blocking.** The attack as verified by experiment on both crypto providers: a fail-open envelope whose `wrap_k` carries a key unrelated to the `m` in `wrap_m` passes the dispatcher (it holds no key), the Mediator opens and judges the `wrap_m` plaintext, `releaseEnvelope` hands readers the sender's `wrap_k` unchanged, and readers derive a different key — with a payload crafted to open under both keys (the AEAD is not key-committing) they would read other words than the Mediator judged. Fail-closed is **not** affected (the Mediator builds the readers' wrap from the `m` it decrypted); Relay originals are never released; reactions are unaffected; **edits inherit it twice**. No reader-subset split is possible once the two wraps are shown equal. **D 48 (launching) ships the stopgap under three conditions:** `checkSenderWrapK` before any PASS on every fail-open user message of every kind, at the single decision point, with `K_e` fetched in parallel with the decrypt; a mismatch is a signed BLOCK (`integrity.wrap_mismatch`, no send-anyway — the fail-open timer releases only from `sent`, so the window closes), counted, alerted, fed to account risk; a missing `K_e` on a fail-open envelope is a HOLD, never a release. **Permanent fix: envelope v2 with a key commitment** in the signed, AEAD-bound header (`BLAKE2b-256(key = m, TBS(key-commit, aad))`), verified by the Mediator from `wrap_m` and by every reader from `wrap_k` — **B 33 on Fable** (core format), gated like the outcome notes. Should-fix: the legacy per-device-wraps epoch form can omit the Mediator wrap at a mediated level (C — the way a member could starve the check), `mediatorOpenEdit` documents a same-author check it does not perform (B), the finding is not yet in `gated-release.md` (invariant G18), `docs/05` §3.2 or ADR-0009 (B 33), the edit-mark rule needs named tests (E1, D). **Rule:** C's and E1's halves of the messaging basics do not merge before D 48 ships the check. Sound: the gate in fail-closed for every new kind, reactions and edits inheriting the gate by construction, content-free dispatcher rules with vectors, signatures by the right parties for deletes and forwards.

The apps bind to `belucid.chat`: bundle id `chat.belucid` in the server default and the native config (`app.json` still carries the old id — L425-F8-F1 before the first EAS build), universal links `applinks:belucid.chat` / `app.belucid.chat`, Android App Links for `/i/` and `/join/`, API `https://api.belucid.chat`, gateway `wss://ws.belucid.chat/v1/ws`, invite links `https://belucid.chat/i/`; the `.well-known` association files are served by every role and list no app until `APPLE_TEAM_ID` / `ANDROID_CERT_SHA256` arrive (card 0eo). The lead redeploys staging from main now so the files go live (the first staging release since A 56 — it carries C 41, D 44–46, F 47 and the A 58 config). Open: the server's invite route `/i/` and the app's `/join/` do not match (L425-F8-F3, C and E1); the SMS provider template must end with `@belucid.chat #<code>` for domain-bound OTP (F4). decisions.title: Positioning: Lucid is an augmented communication app.
decisions.summary: Positioning: Lucid is an augmented communication app.
decisions.text: Positioning: **Lucid is an augmented communication app.** The core message is that Lucid augments, enhances and improves how people communicate with each other; mediation is one mechanism of an augmented communication environment, not the headline. The public website (L446) is rebuilt around this concept: hero, structure, feature narrative and copy lead with augmentation, with the Mediator, Coach, clarity, translation, protections and the Assistant presented as the mechanisms that deliver it. Lead note: the same wording is to be carried into the one-line descriptions in `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/00-system-definition.md` §1 and the store-listing texts (0es) when those are next touched; row WEB-1-F1.

decisions.title: Device runs under watch.
decisions.summary: Device runs under watch.
decisions.text: Device runs under watch. The wave 24 G emulator run held the device slot for over an hour and blocked other suites, and the machine climbed to about 15 GB used, "which makes no sense": find out whether the app leaks or something else does; the emulator is to be configured with less RAM, because Lucid must work well on older devices; from now on every device run is monitored for progress and memory, the app's behaviour is checked, and testing takes a reasonable time. The iOS simulator has not run yet; it runs when RAM is available, after the Android pass. Lead decisions under it: AND-LOW moves from 4 GB to **3 GB** RAM (`hw.ramSize=3072`, matrix §2.1 change approved); per-flow and per-run time caps locally as in CI (6 min / 45 min defaults), an emulator RSS cap and a machine free-memory cap, each configurable; a monitor CSV and a "Memory and time" section in every device walkthrough. Brief `docs/briefs/wave60-A.md` (rows L449-F1…F3); wave 59 A (first iOS run) follows it; waves 24 G and 35 E1 resume after it merges.

(3) **PR walkthroughs move to the 3 GB AVD** (L449-F2-F1): `lucid-pixel-7-api35` (AND-LOW, 3072 MB) becomes the default AVD for device walkthroughs and the Android pass; the API 37 AVD (which emulator 37.2.12 forces to 4 GB) stays for the "API current" check at each gate. (4) **Wave 24 G's 26 flows**: two runs per locale under the 45-minute cap rather than a raised cap. decisions.title: Editing one's own message is a right of the person, not of the device.
decisions.summary: Editing one's own message is a right of the person, not of the device.
decisions.text: **Editing one's own message is a right of the person, not of the device.** The same-author check compares the sender's user identity: a person may edit their own message from any current device, including after the device that sent it was revoked (what every mainstream messenger does). Core `mediatorOpenEdit` takes `target.senderUserId` (from the store) and `target.editorUserId`; the device-set form of wave 33 B stays as a fallback for one release (P1-B-w34-F1). Residual for a Fable wave if wanted: the Mediator trusts the dispatcher's `sender_user_id` (readers re-check against the roster, P1-B-w34-F2). Also in wave 34 B: `Edit.suggestion_ref` (field 4) so a held edit can earn ✎; `blocks.visibility` follows `blocks.blocked_sender_mark`; `keys.legacy-form` check; the consent live notice `ConversationUpdate.auto_session_consent` (15) behind feature 34 (`AUTO_SESSION_NOTICES`); live conformance 61 checks, 60 pass, 1 allowed skip until C advertises 34.

decisions.title: Nudge sensitivity is a shift, not an absolute.
decisions.summary: Nudge sensitivity is a shift, not an absolute.
decisions.text: **Nudge sensitivity is a shift, not an absolute.** `engine.tuning.nudge_sensitivity` moves each guard category's nudge threshold by the table row's distance from the base, so the per-category tuning of the schema is kept, `medium` changes nothing, and holds, blocks, conveyances and reader protections never move (P1-D-w50-F1 closed). Wave 50 D also put L454's same-author rule into the Mediator (the device-set fallback stays until C carries `edit_target.sender_user_id`, wave 45 C), ✎ on a held edit through `Edit.suggestion_ref`, and the forward reader from `@lucid/policy`.

decisions.title: Slow mode exempts owners and admins by default.
decisions.summary: Slow mode exempts owners and admins by default.
decisions.text: **Slow mode exempts owners and admins by default.** Every mainstream messenger with a slow mode (Telegram, Discord) exempts the people who run the group, so Lucid does too: F adds `groups.member_controls.slow_mode.exempt_admins` (default `true`, market layer) and C reads it (P1-C-w45-CR2 → F then C); until then admins are spaced like members on dev only. Also in wave 45 C: the consent notice is emitted (feature 34 advertised; live conformance 61 / 61, 0 skip), the edit's sender id rides the job (L454 now holds end to end), join approval and slow mode are enforced (draft.29, migration 0044 applied on dev and staging), the media test's policy values pass the slow-ask coherence rule.

decisions.text: **The Android pass is done**: E1's 26 flows (28 after two splits) run in en and he on the 3 GB emulator, 27 / 28 pass per locale; the two failures are app defects, not flows (P2-H-10-F10-F4: agreeing again to a changed consent text does not record it; F5: the Assistant cannot create a group), both to E1 36. Findings and decisions: (1) the machine stood still for 5–19 minutes six times during the runs (idle sleep); **every device run now runs under `caffeinate -i`** (A: the routine does it itself, row P2-H-10-F10-F6 with wave 59 A). (2) The emulator's host memory grows with run length, not with the app (190–287 MB per flow, no leak), and met the RAM + 5 GB cap after 29–39 minutes: long flow sets run as **three runs of about nine flows**, never one long run; `--each` / `--resume` are the tools. (3) The first iOS run (wave 59 A, L449-F4) starts now, under the same monitor.

decisions.text: **The first iOS run is done** (wave 59 A, Fable continuation): the ten default flows pass 10 / 10 in en-US and he-IL on the iPhone 18 Pro simulator, iOS 27.0, Xcode 27.1, headless under the monitor; no app defect; the app's memory flat (PSS ≈ 490 MB at rest, 650 peak, back to 490). Found and fixed on the way: Expo SDK 58's precompiled `expo-camera` was ahead of the pinned `expo-modules-core` (dyld abort at launch; the SDK patch set aligned), unsigned simulator builds have no keychain entitlement (the routine signs ad hoc), the iOS memory cap default is 8192 MB (the simulator's processes measure 4.3–5.6 GB), Xcode 27 shows a device only through Device Hub. Confirmed: the status tick is visible to XCTest (ENV-F1-F11 done); iOS Hermes lacks the same five Intl APIs as Android. iOS is part of every user-facing wave's acceptance from now (docs/14 §5); 31 rows re-verdicted from "iOS blocked" to "iOS run due". Wave 25 G runs the full pass of every flow on both platforms next.

decisions.text: **EVAL-DB-1 is built** (wave 47 D, Fable as the labeller): 1 500 new real-text records from open-licence corpora (300 per language), a sealed 125-record held-out split, agreement with the human reference κ 0.971, and the first real-text measurement of the guards — Gemma 4 (routed) recall 0.84 / false-positive rate 0.13, Hebrew 0.70 / 0.15; Mistral Small 3.2 0.86 / 0.20; Qwen3.6 0.80 / 0.11 — **every guard misses the gate bar on real text that the synthetic sets scored perfectly**; spend USD 0.82. Consequences: the Quality page (wave 52 D) shows synthetic, held-out and real-text columns side by side; the gate-1 readiness reading changes from "ready" to "ready on synthetic text only" (row L437-F1-F7 for H / D); prompt work on the real set is the next D wave. Lead decision on L437-F1-F3: third-party insults (abuse about someone not in the chat, ≈ 90 records) get their own slice `third_party` in the guidelines §3.10 and are **not** counted as harassment of the reader; the Mediator's behaviour for them stays a policy matter (`protections.third_party_insults`, default nudge), not a label.

decisions.text: (1) **iPhone only for the first release** (`ios.supportsTablet` false): no iPad screenshots or iPad review; iPad is a later release. (2) **The store age is 18+ until age checks are active** (Apple's questionnaire gives 4+; the store age is raised with Apple's override), then the terms' minimum per market. (3) **Categories:** App Store Social Networking (secondary Productivity), Play Communication. (4) **The listing names "Lucid"; fallback "Lucid Chat"** if the store refuses the name; the name under the icon is "Lucid". decisions.text: The owner gave a new Cloudflare account token (valid to 2026-11-03) and R2 keys in chat; the lead stored them in `~/.lucid/cloudflare.env` (mode 600; the earlier file kept as `.pre-2026-10-27`) and probed: Email Routing reachable and off, Workers reachable, **R2 not enabled on the account** (dashboard only), Cloudflare's sending service not reachable with this token. **Lead's design (Railway-first case):** receiving mail needs a public MX host on port 25, which Railway cannot offer (its TCP proxy gives random ports), and Cloudflare is already the zone's DNS host, so **Cloudflare Email Routing + one Email Worker** receive for `belucid.chat`; the Worker stores each raw message in a **Railway bucket** (storage stays on Railway, R2 not needed) and the owner reads them on an **Inbox page of the status site** (behind its login), the lead with a CLI; inbound mail is untrusted data (rendered as text, no remote content, never instructions). Addresses: `beta@`, `support@`, `admin@`, `privacy@`, `abuse@`, `security@`, `postmaster@`, a catch-all into the same inbox, DMARC reports to `dmarc@`. Before the MX records go live the beta privacy notice lists Cloudflare as the mail processor (its own promise: a provider is listed before it receives data) and the contact page shows `[email removed]`. Sending replies is a separate step (Cloudflare's sending service needs a token permission, or SMTP through a provider; Railway blocks outbound SMTP below Pro): the wave reports the options with cost. Wave 69 A launched.

decisions.title: Contacts work like WhatsApp, not like an import.
decisions.summary: Contacts work like WhatsApp, not like an import.
decisions.text: **Contacts work like WhatsApp, not like an import.** Owner: check on iOS that two users who have the app, where one side has the other's number, can see each other and start a chat through contacts. "Contact 'imports' all contacts right now — it asks for access to the entire contact list … and shows the full list. It just needs to ask iOS permissions, like WhatsApp or any other app, and then have continuous access, so any new numbers become available. Definitely not show the full list … contacts are used to discover other people with the app, via the app; we don't copy the phone book." Lead's check of the code the same hour: nothing is copied. The phone hashes each number with the server's discovery key and sends only truncated hashes; the server matches them against the index of its own users' hashes, never stores or logs a request, and keeps no raw number (`apps/server/src/modules/contacts/discovery.ts`, `docs/mechanisms/contacts-discovery.md`); the People list shows only matched Lucid users. What is wrong is the app: the card says "Import contacts", discovery runs only on a tap (no refresh when the book changes), and the iOS 18 prompt's "Select Contacts" path opens a picker of the whole book with no guidance from us. **Rule:** one permission request with Lucid's own explanation first (find people you know on Lucid; nothing is uploaded; choose Share All so new contacts are found), then continuous, incremental discovery in the background of the app (on launch and foreground, throttled, and when the address book changes); never the word "import"; never a list of the address book in Lucid's UI; limited access handled with a way to Full access in Settings. Wave 40 E1 launched; the two-user one-sided test on two iOS simulators against staging is its acceptance. **Addendum (owner, same hour):** "I have never ever seen the entire contact list surfaced in that way. If it's a new iOS 27 feature, fine, but this was never the case before and I do not want to show it unless we absolutely have no other choice." The wave first identifies which surface listed the book (ours, expo-contacts calling a picker, or the OS on the plain request) with screenshots; Lucid never lists the book or calls a picker, and asks only through the plain system authorization after its own explanation.

decisions.text: (1) "You said we have 1 800 — I want that actually used, and to see performance and rating: significant numbers." (2) "Even that seems small — do another pass and find better sources; I am sure they exist." (3) "Yes, we label with Opus — it's state of the art." (4) "Generate more examples; they are much too few for a proper evaluation." (5) "Go much more deeply into normal conversation use cases, into translation, especially cross-cultural, into moderation and mediation. Make up a lot of conversations, long ones, and we don't just test the single use-case turn: this needs to exist within a true, sustained and long context." Lead's facts behind the answer: the tuning sets are 16–116 records per task, the comparison slices of classify / translate / rephrase are 3–8 records, the guard held-out sets about 820 records, all agent-written; EVAL-DB v1 holds 1 806 records (1 500 from licensed open corpora) and has not been run across the engines; labeller agreement was never measured. **The programme (all on Opus 5.5, launched as the agent cap frees slots):** **55 D** runs every routed and failover engine on all 1 806 EVAL-DB records (measurement only: no prompt is tuned from the held-out split, which keeps wave 53 D's later measurement valid; aggregates only for held-out), with 95 % intervals, per language and class, inside the providers' daily caps (resumable over days), and the Quality page shows *n* and the interval beside every number and greys any figure on fewer than 30 records; **56 D** a second, deeper source pass (licensed corpora for every task: abuse, scams, manipulation, self-harm, translation with cross-cultural content, everyday conversation, ambiguity, chat summaries) into EVAL-DB v2, labelled by Opus with two independent labels per record and agreement (κ) measured; **57 D** the long-conversation evaluation: a schema for long multi-turn conversations with labelled target turns and windows, contrastive pairs (the same turn after different histories), and a harness that replays each conversation turn by turn through the Mediator with the context the product gives it, scoring every turn (interventions, false alarms per 100 benign turns, first-detection delay for patterns that build over days, translation against references and a rubric); **58 D a–d** four writers of long conversations to that schema — everyday conversation, cross-cultural translation, moderation, mediation — about 150 each, many over 150 turns, in en / he / ar / ru / es and mixed pairs, then a blind relabel by a different agent. Out of scope everywhere: any sexual content involving minors; grooming of minors is not written. Engine runs stay inside Scaleway's daily caps; raising a cap is the owner's console step and is asked only if the schedule needs it.

decisions.title: Wave 54 D merged (113b42f9).

decisions.text: **Wave 54 D merged** (113b42f9). The pre-registered failover rule found no engine passing the latency gate, Gemma included, in a slow Scaleway afternoon (every engine 1.3–2× slower than two days before on the same records); the lead keeps the routed chain unchanged (Gemma 4 · v8 → Mistral · v4 → Qwen3.6 · v4) and the re-measurement is P1-D-w54-F1. By answer quality Qwen3.8 · v8 is the best candidate (0.996 recall on answered records) but timed out 10.7 %; it enters the chain only after a passing re-measure and the owner's raise of its daily limit (P1-D-w54-F2). The media read is bound to the message's conversation (P1-C-w18-F8, refusal fails by the conversation's mode). Lead verification: build, typecheck, lint 57 / 57; the whole graph failed 4 packages under machine load (5-minute load up to 107 with six agents and the iOS simulator) — policy, admin, mobile timeouts and one server assertion beside two timeouts — and all four pass alone (policy 642, server 817, mobile 724, admin 536). Owner the same hour on wave 69 A's mail test: "you sent many test messages, stop, I see them" — the lead stopped the sending; forwarding is confirmed by the owner's inbox; remaining failure-path checks run without mailing him.

decisions.title: (1) "The new data and extended testing MUST find and highlight differences between the engines, on performance, quality etc.
decisions.summary: (1) "The new data and extended testing MUST find and highlight differences between the engines, on performance, quality etc.
decisions.text: (1) "The new data and extended testing MUST find and highlight differences between the engines, on performance, quality etc. If they remain consistent with the low-volume tests, then something is not working correctly in our testing": the runs report each engine's strengths and weaknesses by class, language and source with intervals, and a near-identical result is treated as a harness fault to investigate (own-model response ids, no shared cache or parse, no label leak, hand-checked records) — sent to waves 55 D and 57 D. (2) Input and output token counts and costs for all engines, from the providers' usage fields, machine-readable. (3) "A quick back-of-the-envelope estimation … cost at 100 k users, with clear estimated message counts, on a variety of features — with significant context, with the ability to do a local on-device RAG": **wave 59 D**, a cost model page with every assumption sourced and editable. (4) "See if we can leverage iOS's built-in AI capabilities, measure their performance, and see if they can be used instead of cloud servers, at least for supporting devices and at least for some capabilities": **wave AI-2**, Apple's on-device stack (Foundation Models, Translation, NaturalLanguage embeddings, on-device speech) researched with Apple's documents, measured on our eval sets on this Mac and the iOS simulator, and placed against the architecture — on-device output can serve the device's own user (reader translation, summaries, Coach, Assistant planning, on-device retrieval, voice transcription, a sender-side pre-check) but cannot replace the Mediator's verdict that gates release (ADR-0009: the server cannot trust a client's verdict in a fail-closed conversation); the saving feeds the cost model. Both queued behind the six running agents. **Addendum (owner, same hour):** test Gemini Nano too, on the same cases as the other engines ("a little useful and grow over time … let's see if they are good enough for anything"); the owner enabled Apple Intelligence on the build machine. AI-2 tests Apple's on-device model through the macOS harness and Gemini Nano through Chrome's built-in AI on this Mac (Gemma 3n locally only as a labelled proxy if Chrome cannot run it); Android device steps as rows. AI-2 is first in the queue.

decisions.title: (1) Tiered cascade as an architectural principle.
decisions.summary: (1) Tiered cascade as an architectural principle.
decisions.text: (1) **Tiered cascade as an architectural principle.** "Use the fast and less capable models to answer quickly and do things within their ability, and move to stronger models if there's ambiguity, or in tasks and cases where a stronger model would be far better — for both cost and response time." If the on-device models perform passably, "notably if they have low false negatives", they serve as quick triage and pass on to stronger models. "We get more false positives with weaker models, so when there's a positive we likely want to pass it into stronger judgement." (2) **Nuanced evaluation:** "not just positive or negative — the model's ability to explain the issue, or to culturally translate, or to intelligently mediate while keeping to the core guidance; not leaking information when mediating." (3) **Two mediators:** "likely only doable where there really are two mediators, each knowing what the limits are of the other side, and negotiating with the other side's model to optimize the joint mediation response; test this approach vs single-model mediation, ensuring we never leak secrets or private things said to the model, and never share without explicit consent." (4) "All of the above must be reflected in the docs and then added and performed as tasks." **Lead's plan:** **ARCH-3** (design, ADR-0024 *tiered inference cascade*): triage → escalation stages per task, escalation on a positive, on low confidence or abstention, on task-difficulty classes and on policy; the on-device tier (wave AI-2) as the first stage for the device's own user, never as the release gate (ADR-0009); every threshold a platform-policy setting; the cascade as a registry construct; the fail-open window and latency SLOs (ADR-0023, `docs/06`); cascade simulation in every eval run; docs 02, 04, 06, 11, 13 updated. **MED-2** (design, ADR-0025 *party-private mediation*): a per-party mediator holding only its party's private context and limits, a negotiation protocol between the two, a joint response built only from what each side consented to share, information-flow labels on every private item, an outgoing leak check, explicit consent before anything private is shared, and the comparison with single-model mediation under a red-team leakage suite; docs 02, 04, 05, 11, 12 updated. **60 D** (evaluation): rubric scoring of explanations, cultural translation, mediation quality and adherence to the core guidance, judge calibration against Opus reference grades, the leakage suite with canaries and probing, and the cascade simulation over every engine's per-record results (quality, cost, latency and escalation rate per triage–escalation pair) on the Quality page. Then build rows: the cascade in the router and registry (D with C), the on-device triage tier (E1 with D), the two-mediator prototype measured against the single model (D). ARCH-3 and MED-2 are document waves and start now, beside the six running agents.

decisions.title: ADR-0024 accepted (the tiered inference cascade, ARCH-3 merged).
decisions.summary: ADR-0024 accepted (the tiered inference cascade, ARCH-3 merged).
decisions.text: **ADR-0024 accepted** (the tiered inference cascade, ARCH-3 merged). Reviewed against L492: the device never releases (its sealed, content-free hint can only stop a speculative escalation in a fail-open conversation and costs only latency if forged); positives from an over-flagging stage always escalate; a cheaper stage closes negatives only under a per-run certificate (the exact 95 % upper bound of its false-negative rate under the policy threshold per class and language, held-out and sealed records only, voided by a model or prompt change, a 2 % live audit on the anchor withdrawing rights); every threshold is under `ai.cascade.*`, master switch off. Honest consequence: no class × language cell can be certified on today's sets (≈ 60 abusive records per language), so the cascade ships with empty rights and earns them as EVAL-DB v2 and the long conversations grow (waves 56–58 D). Its finding that today's second opinion (Mistral Small 3.2) is weaker than the Gemma guard it second-guesses goes to wave 60 D's slice check (L492-F15) before any policy change. Build rows L492-F5, F7–F15 are in `docs/15`.

decisions.title: ADR-0025 accepted as the design to build and measure (party-private mediation, MED-2 merged).
decisions.summary: ADR-0025 accepted as the design to build and measure (party-private mediation, MED-2 merged).
decisions.text: **ADR-0025 accepted as the design to build and measure** (party-private mediation, MED-2 merged). The lead's answers to its §11 questions, small enough to decide (L425): (1) "each knowing what the limits are of the other side" is read as each mediator holding its own party's limits and knowing what the other side may and may not reveal; the literal single-model reading is one of the four comparison arms, so the measurement settles it. (2) Session-scoped `PARTY_PRIVATE` records readable by the Mediator only while the session lives, with the Mediator's key copy deleted at its end, are transit context like Relay originals and sit **outside** L437's "no Mediator-held memory" (nothing is kept for later use). (3) The outcome leak (what an agreed result implies about a limit) is accepted once disclosed to the party before the session; counsel reviews the wording under G28. The leak check failing closed is an invariant, not a setting; nothing private is shared without the owner's signed tap on the exact text; which arm ships is decided only by the pre-registered rule (zero exact canary leaks and full leaks ≤ 1 % at the 95 % upper bound with ≥ 300 planted pairs per language; two mediators unless the single model matches and is ≥ 30 % cheaper or 1 s faster; neither passes → the feature stays off). The prototype and measurement are L492-F6; the mocks are E2's (nine frames, the `share-consent` glyph).
